section_title: Virtual Control Groups and Data Reuse as Reduction

findings.claim: In 306 oncology papers, only 48% of articles under a blanket mandatory data-sharing policy actually made data available, and none of six under a mandatory code-sharing policy shared code.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Less than half of the 29 articles that were subject to a blanket mandatory data sharing policy were observed to make data available (14/29, 48%, 95% CI: 31–66%). Furthermore, of the six studies that performed inferential statistics and were subjected to a blanket mandatory code sharing policy, none reported sharing code.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Less than half of the 29 articles that were subject to a blanket mandatory data sharing policy were observed to make data available (14/29, 48%, 95% CI: 31–66%).
findings.study_system: 306 cancer-related journal articles indexed in PubMed 2019

findings.claim: The Open Data Commons for Spinal Cord Injury (a FAIR repository for long-tail preclinical data) had 248 registered users and 57 labs by July 2020.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As of July 2020, 248 users are registered on the site and 57 different laboratories across Canada, Europe and USA have been created.
findings.effect_size: 248 users; 57 laboratories
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: As of July 2020, 248 users are registered on the site and 57 different laboratories across Canada, Europe and USA have been created.
findings.study_system: Preclinical spinal cord injury data-sharing repository (odc-sci.org)

findings.claim: Despite the BMJ's strong data-sharing policy, only 4.5% of 157 sampled research articles actually made raw data easily available.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The percentage of data easily available from the 157 articles was only 4.5% (95% CI 1.8% to 9%).
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The percentage of data easily available from the 157 articles was only 4.5% (95% CI 1.8% to 9%).
findings.study_system: BMJ research articles 2009-2015 (data-sharing audit)

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 105 meta-research studies found only ~8% of 2016-2021 medical papers declared public data availability and just 2% actually shared data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Aggregation of the findings of sufficiently similar studies suggested that on average, 8% of medical papers published between 2016 and 2021 declared that their data were publicly available and 2% actually shared their data publicly.
findings.effect_size: 8% declared; 2% actual
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Aggregation of the findings of sufficiently similar studies suggested that on average, 8% of medical papers published between 2016 and 2021 declared that their data were publicly available and 2% actually shared their data publicly.
findings.study_system: Systematic review/meta-analysis of data & code sharing in medicine

findings.claim: A systematic review of FAIR-supporting initiatives for precision oncology narrowed references to 60 for full-text analysis, then recommended existing standards (GDC, ICD, HGVS).
findings.claim_source_sentence: A full-text review was then performed on 60 references.
findings.effect_size: 60 references
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A full-text review was then performed on 60 references.
findings.study_system: Precision oncology FAIR data-sharing initiatives (systematic literature review)

findings.claim: MicrO, an OBO-Foundry microbiology ontology, reuses >12,000 terms imported from 19 other OBO ontologies, linked by >24,130 logical axioms.
findings.claim_source_sentence: MicrO incorporates more than 12,000 additional relevant terms from 19 other ontologies in the OBO Foundry Library and these imported terms are connected to MicrO classes using a large number of logical axioms (over 24,130, with 5,446 specific to MicrO).
findings.effect_size: >12,000 imported terms; 19 ontologies; >24,130 axioms
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: MicrO incorporates more than 12,000 additional relevant terms from 19 other ontologies in the OBO Foundry Library and these imported terms are connected to MicrO classes using a large number of logical axioms (over 24,130, with 5,446 specific to MicrO).
findings.study_system: Prokaryotic phenotype/metabolic ontology (MicrO), OBO Foundry

findings.claim: The OBO Foundry was created to counter ontology proliferation, coordinating reform of ontologies (including the Gene Ontology) under shared development principles to enable data integration.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Unfortunately, the very success of this approach has led to a proliferation of ontologies, which itself creates obstacles to integration.
findings.study_system: Open Biomedical Ontologies (OBO) Foundry

findings.claim: The FaceBase craniofacial data repository shows a self-curation model can deliver FAIR, reusable data at scale.
findings.claim_source_sentence: FaceBase demonstrates that a model in which researchers "self-curate" their data can be successful and scalable.
findings.study_system: Craniofacial/dental FAIR data repository (FaceBase Consortium)

findings.claim: ImmuneData unifies five NIAID immunology repositories (ImmPort, ImmuneSpace, ITN TrialShare, ImmGen, IEDB) under one ontology-driven schema to support FAIR data reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The system provides integrated access to five immunology data repositories funded by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, Division of Allergy, Immunology and Transplantation, including ImmPort, ImmuneSpace, ITN TrialShare, ImmGen and IEDB.
findings.effect_size: five repositories
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The system provides integrated access to five immunology data repositories funded by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, Division of Allergy, Immunology and Transplantation, including ImmPort, ImmuneSpace, ITN TrialShare, ImmGen and IEDB.
findings.study_system: Immunology data discovery across five repositories (ImmuneData)

findings.claim: Despite billions in public investment in nanosafety research, reuse of accumulated nanosafety data lags, motivating a FAIR-aligned Nanosafety Data Interface.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Nanotechnology is a key enabling technology with billions of euros in global investment from public funding, which include large collaborative projects that have investigated environmental and health safety aspects of nanomaterials, but the reuse of accumulated data is clearly lagging behind.
findings.study_system: Nanosafety data (physicochemical, toxicity, omics, exposure)

findings.claim: Of 79 otolaryngology journals with data-sharing policies, 91% required globally unique persistent metadata identifiers but there were clear gaps in accessibility and reusability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Seventy-two policies (of 79; 91%) designated that metadata should have globally unique and persistent identifiers.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Seventy-two policies (of 79; 91%) designated that metadata should have globally unique and persistent identifiers.
findings.study_system: Otolaryngology journal data-sharing policies vs FAIR principles

findings.claim: Of 1792 papers whose data-availability statement promised sharing, 93% of authors did not respond or declined, and only 6.8% provided data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Among 1792 manuscripts in which the DAS indicated that authors are willing to share their data, 1669 (93%) authors either did not respond or declined to share their data with us.
findings.effect_size: 1669/1792, 93% did not share
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Among 1792 manuscripts in which the DAS indicated that authors are willing to share their data, 1669 (93%) authors either did not respond or declined to share their data with us.
findings.study_system: Data-availability statements in 333 BioMed Central open-access journals

findings.claim: Among 1,084 articles in top orthopaedic journals (2020-2023) only 14% carried a data-sharing statement, and just 12 of 115 contacted authors agreed to share.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of the 1,084 reviewed articles, only 14% included a DSS.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 1,084 reviewed articles, only 14% included a DSS.
findings.study_system: Top orthopaedic journals data-sharing statements (2020-2023)

findings.claim: In leading gastroenterology journals (2018-2023), 42% of 953 articles contained a data-sharing statement, with journals with mandatory policies showing higher compliance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of the 953 articles that met inclusion criteria, 400 (400/953; 42.0%) contained a DSS.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 953 articles that met inclusion criteria, 400 (400/953; 42.0%) contained a DSS.
findings.study_system: Gastroenterology journal data-sharing statements (2018-2023)

findings.claim: A critique argues that universal mandatory raw-data-sharing mandates are ill-suited to qualitative research and can harm rigorous, ethical practice.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, we argue that universal open raw data mandates cannot adequately represent the diversity of qualitative research, and that MIRD may harm rigorous and ethical research practice within health psychology and beyond.
findings.study_system: Mandatory data-sharing policy critique (qualitative health-psychology research)

findings.claim: A systematic review frames the absence of career incentives (beyond publication/citation counts) as the rate-limiting barrier to biomedical data sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The lack of incentives has been described as the rate-limiting step for data sharing.
findings.study_system: Incentive mechanisms for biomedical data sharing (systematic review)

findings.claim: The eTRANSAFE IMI consortium produced FAIR data-sharing and model-verification guidelines to integrate curated and newly generated preclinical drug-safety data across partners.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The research reproducibility guidelines presented in this study lay the foundation for a comprehensive data sharing and knowledge management plans accounting for research data management in the drug safety space - FAIR data sharing guidelines, and the model verification guidelines as generic deliverables that best practices that can be reused by other scientific community members at large.
findings.study_system: Translational drug-safety data integration (eTRANSAFE, IMI)

findings.claim: A student reanalysis of six PRIDE proteomics deposits found systemic metadata/format gaps produced large discrepancies (13,068 vs 4,923 proteins), showing open-access deposition does not guarantee reusability ('data tombs').
findings.claim_source_sentence: In contrast, the team's search identified 13,068 unique proteins after filtering.
findings.effect_size: 13,068 (reanalysis) vs 4,923 (original) proteins
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast, the team's search identified 13,068 unique proteins after filtering.
findings.study_system: Reanalysis of six public PRIDE proteomics projects

findings.claim: Embedding Schema.org/JSON-LD machine-readable metadata (with DDI and OMOP CDM) made population-health datasets from Malawi and Kenya discoverable via generic search engines, improving FAIRness and reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our structured representation methodology makes the IDSR data set easily discoverable through platforms such as Google Dataset Search.
findings.study_system: Population-health surveillance data (Malawi, Kenya); machine-readable metadata + OMOP

findings.claim: An open-science drug-discovery data roadmap argues robust reuse requires precise ontologies and standardized vocabularies plus centralized, mine-able electronic lab notebooks.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Robust data management requires precise ontologies and standardized vocabulary while a centralized database architecture across laboratories facilitates data integration into high-value datasets.
findings.study_system: Open-science early-stage drug discovery data management (SGC roadmap)

findings.claim: A published dataset deposited HLA-A nanopore sequencing for 64 people living with HIV (32 with, 32 without periodontitis) in NCBI SRA and Figshare explicitly to enable reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The dataset includes nanopore sequencing data (FASTQ format) for HLA-A alleles obtained from 64 PLWH participants (32 with periodontitis and 32 without).
findings.effect_size: 64 participants
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The dataset includes nanopore sequencing data (FASTQ format) for HLA-A alleles obtained from 64 PLWH participants (32 with periodontitis and 32 without).
findings.study_system: HLA-A/periodontitis dataset in SRA + Figshare (data reuse example)

findings.claim: The INSPIRE project integrated heterogeneous longitudinal African mental-health data into a staging database using DDI-Lifecycle and OMOP CDM vocabularies to enable standardized sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Adherence to metadata standards ensures data quality, promotes interoperability, and expands opportunities for data sharing in mental health research.
findings.study_system: Longitudinal mental-health data harmonization (INSPIRE, DDI + OMOP)

findings.claim: A clinical-research-informatics review of 517 papers concluded the field's dominant thrust is real-world-evidence generation through reuse of EHR data, enabled by OMOP-style semantic interoperability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The most significant research efforts in the CRI field are currently focusing on real world evidence generation and especially the reuse of EHR data.
findings.study_system: Clinical research informatics field survey (EHR data reuse, OMOP)

findings.claim: A systematic assessment of 253 omics studies (164,000+ samples) found public metadata is markedly incomplete: on average only 74.8% of important phenotypes were shared, limiting reuse and reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We observed that studies often omit over a quarter of important phenotypes, with an average of only 74.8% of them shared either in the text of publication or the corresponding repository.
findings.effect_size: 74.8% of phenotypes shared
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We observed that studies often omit over a quarter of important phenotypes, with an average of only 74.8% of them shared either in the text of publication or the corresponding repository.
findings.study_system: Metadata completeness of omics studies in Gene Expression Omnibus

findings.claim: OpenNeuro (a FAIR, BIDS-standard neuroimaging archive) shares more than 600 datasets from over 20,000 participants and documents more than 150 published reuses, providing rare direct evidence that standardized deposition yields downstream reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The impact of the shared data is evident in a growing number of published reuses, currently totalling more than 150 publications.
findings.effect_size: more than 150 reuse publications; >600 datasets; >20,000 participants
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The impact of the shared data is evident in a growing number of published reuses, currently totalling more than 150 publications.
findings.study_system: OpenNeuro FAIR neuroimaging data archive (BIDS standard)

findings.claim: A systematic review of COVID-19 datasets found only 28.5% of 12,324 PubMed Central full-text articles linked any dataset, with substantial heterogeneity in how datasets were shared, hosted and cited.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that 28.5% of 12 324 COVID-19 full-text articles in PubMed Central provided at least one dataset link.
findings.effect_size: 28.5% of 12,324 articles
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We found that 28.5% of 12 324 COVID-19 full-text articles in PubMed Central provided at least one dataset link.
findings.study_system: COVID-19 dataset sharing in PubMed Central articles (systematic review)

findings.claim: Analysis of GDPR/DGA/EHDS shows EU regulations aim to enable cross-border health-data access and consent-based data altruism, but for rare diseases the secondary-use framework and genomic/biobank exceptions create a fragmented legal landscape.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These regulations open opportunities to enhance cross-border data access, the promotion of data altruism, and the development of data governance models facilitating biomedical research.
findings.study_system: EU health-data regulation (GDPR, Data Governance Act, European Health Data Space) applied to rare-disease research

findings.claim: Because Italy has one of Europe's most restrictive frameworks for genetic data, misaligned regulation means accessing biobank data to train AI systems will be severely limited without reform.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We conclude by arguing that currently, regulatory frameworks are misaligned and unless addressed, accessing data within Italian biobanks to train AI will be severely limited.
findings.study_system: Italian population biobanks; secondary use of biobank data for AI training

findings.claim: An assessment of 27 longitudinal population-health cohorts found data can generally be shared for secondary use, but purposes and preconditions are highly variable, and heterogeneous use conditions impede pooling for common reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The data use and data sharing conditions applicable to 27 population health cohorts were assessed.
findings.effect_size: 27 population-health cohorts assessed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The data use and data sharing conditions applicable to 27 population health cohorts were assessed.
findings.study_system: 27 longitudinal population-health cohorts (consent/governance documents)

findings.claim: An online survey of European biobank professionals probed secondary use of data, re-contacting participants, and sharing with industry, revealing a need to improve informed-consent procedures and legal guidance for data/sample sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We conducted an online survey among biobankers and researchers to investigate secondary use of data, informing and/or re-contacting participants, sharing of data with third parties from industry, participant engagement, and collaboration with industrial partners.
findings.study_system: European biobank professionals (BBMRI network survey)

findings.claim: A content analysis of 30 ethics regulatory documents from 22 African countries found governance frameworks for genomic sample and data sharing were the most sparsely covered aspect, leaving researchers and ethics committees without adequate guidance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We sourced 30 ethics regulatory documents from 22 African countries.
findings.effect_size: 30 ethics regulatory documents from 22 African countries
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We sourced 30 ethics regulatory documents from 22 African countries.
findings.study_system: Ethics guidelines/policies from 22 African countries (genomics & biobanking)

findings.claim: A PRISMA scoping review identified 485 studies on Open Science impacts, reporting mostly positive/mixed effects on citations, reuse and reproducibility, but the main barrier to impact is lack of skills, resources and infrastructure to effectively reuse existing research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We identify 485 studies related to all aspects of OS, including Open Access (OA), Open/FAIR Data (OFD), Open Code/Software, Open Evaluation and Citizen Science (CS).
findings.effect_size: 485 studies synthesized
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We identify 485 studies related to all aspects of OS, including Open Access (OA), Open/FAIR Data (OFD), Open Code/Software, Open Evaluation and Citizen Science (CS).
findings.study_system: Open Science literature (scoping review across OA, open/FAIR data, code, citizen science)

findings.claim: The AgBioData data-reuse working group identified limitations of data standards, metadata deficiencies, poor interoperability, unclear data ownership, and skill/resource gaps as the principal bottlenecks to reuse in agricultural genomics.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Here, we identify the limitations of data standards, metadata deficiencies, data interoperability, data ownership, data availability, user skill level, resource availability, and equity issues, with a specific focus on agricultural genomics research.
findings.study_system: Agricultural genomics/transcriptomics data reuse (AgBioData consortium)

findings.claim: A global-health data-sharing analysis argues sharing efficiency should be measured by the flow of benefits and decision-making authority to disadvantaged regions rather than by the volume or speed of data transfer, reframing mandates around equity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To genuinely advance global health equity, data sharing efficiency should be measured not by the volume or speed of data transfer, but by the deliberate flow of benefits, capacity and decision-making authority to structurally disadvantaged regions.
findings.study_system: Global-health data and biospecimen sharing governance

findings.claim: Reuse of a decade of nanosafety Comet-assay genotoxicity data was hampered by poorly described metadata, non-standard terminology and lack of harmonized reporting formats, motivating FAIRification via the eNanoMapper data model.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite a great amount of nanosafety data having been produced over the last decade in international collaborative initiatives, their interpretation, integration and reuse has been hampered by several obstacles, such as poorly described (meta)data, non-standard terminology, lack of harmonized reporting formats and criteria.
findings.study_system: Nanosafety Comet-assay genotoxicity data (eNanoMapper / Gov4Nano)

findings.claim: linkedISA adds a semantic-web (RDF) layer to ISA-Tab, making experimental metadata machine-processable and mappable to community ontologies so that datasets become reproducible, comparable and reusable.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Reporting and sharing experimental metadata- such as the experimental design, characteristics of the samples, and procedures applied, along with the analysis results, in a standardised manner ensures that datasets are comprehensible and, in principle, reproducible, comparable and reusable.
findings.study_system: ISA-Tab semantic representation (linkedISA / RDF)

findings.claim: ISA-TAB-Nano was created because a lack of standardization means most shared nanomaterial data are incomplete, poorly integrated and unsuitable for meaningful interpretation or reuse or for building predictive models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Owing to the lack of standardization in representing and sharing nanomaterial data, most of the data currently shared via publications and data resources are incomplete, poorly-integrated, and not suitable for meaningful interpretation and re-use of the data.
findings.study_system: Nanomaterial research data sharing (ISA-TAB-Nano spreadsheet standard)

findings.claim: A community consultation in the UK bioimaging field found good imaging-data management remains a major challenge, with a lack of standardized practices and limited training, prompting a three-module curriculum covering metadata, storage/sharing and public-repository submission.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, good data management remains a major challenge across imaging facilities, with lack of standardised practices and limited training opportunities.
findings.study_system: UK bioimaging community (imaging data stewardship survey/curriculum)

findings.claim: The Alliance of Genome Resources unifies seven model-organism knowledgebases plus the Gene Ontology into a shared knowledge commons, using common gene-ortholog assertions to make curated function, phenotype and disease annotations comparable across species.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The Alliance is a consortium of seven model organism knowledgebases (mouse, rat, yeast, nematode, zebrafish, frog, fruit fly) and the Gene Ontology resource.
findings.effect_size: seven model-organism knowledgebases plus the Gene Ontology
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The Alliance is a consortium of seven model organism knowledgebases (mouse, rat, yeast, nematode, zebrafish, frog, fruit fly) and the Gene Ontology resource.
findings.study_system: Alliance of Genome Resources (7 model-organism databases + GO)

findings.claim: A measurement systematic review found that of 60 independent surveys (72 publications) assessing data-sharing knowledge/attitudes/practices, fewer than one-third reported pilot testing and only three reported measurement properties, indicating a weak, non-comparable evidence base.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We screened 3684 title-abstracts, reviewed 104 full texts and extracted data from 72 publications representing 60 independent surveys.
findings.effect_size: 72 publications / 60 independent surveys; only 3 reported measurement properties
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We screened 3684 title-abstracts, reviewed 104 full texts and extracted data from 72 publications representing 60 independent surveys.
findings.study_system: Quantitative surveys of biomedical data-sharing KAP (measurement systematic review, COSMIN)

findings.claim: Across 253 omics studies (164,000 samples) plus an extended set of 61,000 GEO studies, over 25% of critical metadata were omitted and only 11.5% of studies shared all phenotypes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We find that over 25% of critical metadata are omitted, with only 74.8% of relevant phenotypes available in publications or public repositories.
findings.effect_size: 25% metadata omitted; 11.5% studies fully shared; 37.9% shared <40%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Only 11.5% of studies completely shared all phenotypes, while 37.9% shared less than 40% of the phenotypes.
findings.study_system: 253 omics studies (164,000 samples) + extended 61,000 GEO studies (2.1M samples), human and non-human mammalian

findings.claim: In GEO, microarray still comprises ~48% of bacterial transcriptomic entries, and lack of standard formats limits reusability to at least 44% of ~45,000 microarray entries.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Thus, we delve into the availability and processability of bacterial microarray data in GEO, showing a complex panorama where the lack of standard formats limits our reusability potential to at least 44% of the ~45 000 microarray entries.
findings.effect_size: microarray ~48% of bacterial entries; reusable >=44% of ~45,000 entries
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Notwithstanding the accelerated growth in RNA-seq experiments, microarray still accounts for ~48% of bacterial transcriptomic entries in GEO, highlighting the need to revalue this data.
findings.study_system: ~45,000 bacterial microarray entries in Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO)

findings.claim: Despite full embrace of data sharing, proteomics dataset metadata (sample and design level) remains limited, and adoption of the SDRF-Proteomics standard is low with weak incentives and enforcement.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although standards such as Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics) and supporting tools are already available, their adoption remains limited.
findings.study_system: Proteomics community metadata provision / SDRF-Proteomics standard

findings.claim: In solid-tumor proteomics, data availability has not translated into straightforward reuse because heterogeneous design, acquisition, workflows and metadata quality limit reproducibility and cross-study comparability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Nevertheless, data availability has not been translated into straightforward reuse: differences in experimental design, acquisition strategies, quantification workflows and metadata quality still limit the reproducibility and cross-study comparability.
findings.study_system: Solid-tumor (colorectal, prostate) proteomics public repository datasets

findings.claim: Secondary use of public omics data (human embryonic kidney cell lines) is impeded by widespread data-reporting issues, prompting a call to re-evaluate open-access curation and submission procedures.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This paper aims to draw attention to widespread issues with data reporting and encourages data owners to meticulously curate submissions to maximize not only their immediate research impact but also the long-term legacy of datasets.
findings.study_system: Human embryonic kidney (HEK293) cell-line omics data in public repositories

findings.claim: The genomics consensus that human data should be 'broadly' shared rests on imprecise, interchangeable definitions of 'broad', producing inconsistent implementation across landmark studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this Perspective, we identify definitions of broad that have been used interchangeably, despite their distinct implications.
findings.study_system: Human genomic data-sharing policy (six landmark genomics studies)

findings.claim: Neuroscience has shifted from anemic data sharing to largely open science, served by a globally distributed ecosystem of data-type-specialized repositories whose FAIRness requires coordination across many stakeholders.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Neuroscience has made significant strides over the past decade in moving from a largely closed science characterized by anemic data sharing, to a largely open science where the amount of publicly available neuroscience data has increased dramatically.
findings.study_system: Neuroscience data-repository ecosystem (INCF/FAIR infrastructure)

findings.claim: Despite scientific benefits, only a fraction of human brain data is currently shared because of various disincentives.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Sharing human brain data can yield scientific benefits, but because of various disincentives, only a fraction of these data is currently shared.
findings.study_system: NIH BRAIN Initiative Research Opportunities in Humans (ROH) Consortium neurophysiology data

findings.claim: Reuse of human neuroscience data for AI is blocked by cross-country legal heterogeneity and by missing standards for metadata annotation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Finally, it elaborates on the problem of missing standards for metadata annotation and introduces initiatives that aim at developing tools to make neuroscientific data acquisition and analysis pipelines FAIR by design.
findings.study_system: Human neuroscience data sharing (legal frameworks + metadata standards)

findings.claim: GA4GH released a standardized lexicon of data-sharing terms (including 'data visiting' and 'federated data analysis') to reduce inconsistent terminology impeding cross-border genomics collaboration.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To address these barriers, the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH), a global standards-setting organization in genomics, has developed a standardized lexicon of key terms for data sharing, including the nascent terms data visiting and federated data analysis.
findings.study_system: GA4GH genomics data-sharing terminology / governance

findings.claim: The Human Tumor Atlas Network's first phase shared 8,425 biospecimens from 2,042 participants profiled with more than 20 molecular assays via standards, infrastructure and governance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Data from the first phase of the Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) are now available, comprising 8,425 biospecimens from 2,042 research participants profiled with more than 20 molecular assays.
findings.effect_size: 8,425 biospecimens; 2,042 participants; >20 assays
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Data from the first phase of the Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) are now available, comprising 8,425 biospecimens from 2,042 research participants profiled with more than 20 molecular assays.
findings.study_system: Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) multi-omics cancer data

findings.claim: Across four clinical-trial data-sharing platforms, only 25% of data-request proposals were fully concordant with their resulting publications on all three shared characteristics (Vivli: 35/117, 29.9%).
findings.claim_source_sentence: Across four clinical data sharing platforms, data request proposals were often discordant with their corresponding publications, with only 25% concordant across all three key proposal characteristics reported by each platform.
findings.effect_size: 25% fully concordant overall; Vivli 35/117 (29.9%); CSDR 20/106 (18.9%); YODA 15/65 (23.1%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of 117 Vivli publication-request pairs, 76 (65.0%) were fully concordant for the trials requested and analyzed, 61 (52.1%) for study objectives, and 57 (48.7%) for statistical methods; 35 (29.9%) pairs were fully concordant across the 3 characteristics.
findings.study_system: 291 publication-request pairs across Vivli, ClinicalStudyDataRequest.com, Yale Open Data Access, SOAR-BMS

findings.claim: Analyzing ~122,000 publications, sharing data in a repository conferred only a modest 4.3% citation advantage and preprints 20.2%, while sharing code showed no significant advantage.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We also find that sharing data in an online repository correlates with a smaller yet still positive citation advantage of 4.3% (±.8) on average.
findings.effect_size: data +4.3% (+/-.8); preprint +20.2% (+/-.7); code: no significant advantage
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We find that the early release of a publication as a preprint correlates with a significant positive citation advantage of about 20.2% (±.7) on average.
findings.study_system: ~122,000 PLOS + PMC-OA publications 2018-2023 (Open Science Indicators)

findings.claim: Accessing and reusing public untargeted metabolomics data across repositories poses significant challenges, motivating pan-repository universal identifiers and harmonized cross-repository metadata to unlock reanalysis across MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, and GNPS/MassIVE.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Public untargeted metabolomics data is a growing resource for metabolite and phenotype discovery; however, accessing and utilizing these data across repositories pose significant challenges.
findings.evidence: Develops pan-repository identifiers and harmonized metadata to enable cross-repository reanalysis.
findings.study_system: public metabolomics repositories (MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, GNPS/MassIVE)

findings.claim: MetaboLights is a cross-species, cross-technique global metabolomics repository holding raw data and associated metadata, recommended by leading journals and ELIXIR, with community reuse of public data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: MetaboLights is a global database for metabolomics studies including the raw experimental data and the associated metadata.
findings.evidence: Repository description covering standardized workflows (MetaboLights Labs) and documented reuse of public data.
findings.study_system: MetaboLights metabolomics repository

findings.claim: Raw data in major metabolomics repositories lack standardization of file/system formats, making it difficult for non-experts to reuse deposited datasets in downstream analysis platforms; CloMet converts MetaboLights/Metabolomics Workbench data into analysis-ready formats.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Yet, the raw data stored in the aforementioned repositories lack standardization in terms of the file system format used to store the associated acquisition files.
findings.evidence: Open-source converter bridging repositories and analysis platforms to improve reusability and reproducibility.
findings.study_system: metabolomics repositories (MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench) and analysis platforms

findings.claim: SSBD was restructured into a two-tiered resource (a broad repository plus a curated metadata-rich database) to reconcile the conflicting demands of rapid data publication and richly annotated, highly reusable bioimaging data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This update addresses the conflicting demands of rapid data publication and sharing of richly annotated data, thereby promoting bioimaging data sharing and reuse.
findings.evidence: Bioimaging data ecosystem balancing rapid sharing against curated reusability, with metadata harmonization for cross-resource exchange.
findings.study_system: SSBD bioimaging data repository/database

findings.claim: Sharing and standardizing biomedical imaging data across modalities remains a global challenge, driving international efforts to build FAIR, interoperable frameworks bridging biological and clinical imaging communities.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This article examines the global challenges and emerging solutions in sharing and standardizing biomedical imaging data across modalities.
findings.evidence: Perspective on consensus-building and infrastructure for global imaging data interoperability.
findings.study_system: biomedical imaging data-sharing standards

findings.claim: High-content screening generates massive heterogeneous metadata (images, reagents, protocols, analytics, phenotypes) that must be linked and shared, posing a unique data-management challenge addressed via OMERO-based workflow management systems.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, it generates massive amounts of metadata, making HCS experiments a unique data management challenge.
findings.evidence: Reusable semi-automatic workflows for FAIR image data management on OMERO.
findings.study_system: high-content screening bioimaging data management (OMERO)

findings.claim: A systematic review of genomic data-sharing willingness found trust, not factual genomic literacy, was the central determinant, often compensating for limited literacy, while financial considerations played only a minor role.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Trust was a central factor influencing willingness to share data, often compensating for limited genomic literacy.
findings.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 15 empirical studies (2015-2025) on genomic data sharing and health literacy.
findings.effect_size: 15 studies met inclusion criteria
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria.
findings.study_system: systematic review: patient genomic data-sharing willingness

findings.claim: In a 527-participant simulation, altruism and perceived benefit drove willingness to share medical data with researchers while privacy concerns and patient activation reduced it, and demographic factors were not significant predictors.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Altruism and perceived benefit drive willingness to share health data, while privacy concerns and patient activation may reduce it, emphasizing the need for patient-centered, transparent consent models.
findings.evidence: Mixed-methods simulation study (iAgree platform) with logistic regression and thematic analysis.
findings.effect_size: 527 US adults across 4 simulated studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We conducted a mixed-methods study with 527 US adults (≥18 years) recruited via advisory boards, social media, clinics, and newsletters.
findings.study_system: US adults, medical data-sharing consent simulation

findings.claim: Only a quarter of high-impact rehabilitation studies included a data-sharing statement, and when authors who declared data 'available on request' were contacted, follow-through was low.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of the 1,278 studies that underwent data extraction, 326 (25.51%) contained DSS.
findings.evidence: Cross-sectional PRISMA-style audit of 1,278 clinical studies in five top rehabilitation journals (2017-2023), plus email requests to corresponding authors to test willingness to share.
findings.effect_size: 326/1278 (25.51%) contained a data-sharing statement; of 89 responding authors, 43 (48.31%) willing to share unconditionally
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We sent 251 emails to the corresponding authors and received 89 (35.46%) responses within two weeks. Of the 89 respondents, 43 (48.31%) were willing to share de-identified data unconditionally, while 16 (17.98%) were willing to share it only under specific conditions.
findings.study_system: high-impact rehabilitation journal clinical studies, 2017-2023

findings.claim: Coordinated community curation replaced roughly 220 million project-specific variant IDs with standard reference SNP identifiers (rsIDs) to make agricultural genetic-variation data interoperable and reusable, closing a gap where agricultural genomics has lagged human genomics in FAIR practices.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In total, nearly or almost 220 million custom variant IDs were replaced with stable rsIDs: 78.9 million in maize, 67.7 million in rice, 46.4 million in sorghum, 26.3 million in Arabidopsis, and 315,353 in grapevine.
findings.evidence: AgBioData working-group effort brokering submissions to the European Variation Archive and adopting rsIDs across crop pangenome/community databases.
findings.effect_size: ~220 million custom IDs replaced with rsIDs; sorghum community rsIDs rose from 8 million to over 55 million
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In sorghum, the submission of three major studies increased the number of rsIDs available to the community from 8 million in EVA release 3 (February 2022) to over 55 million in release 7 (April 2025).
findings.study_system: agricultural genomics (crops/livestock), European Variation Archive

findings.claim: Among acute-febrile-illness research cohorts, fewer than a quarter used an internationally accepted data standard and documented external-access processes were rare, with technical and regulatory issues rated the most important barriers to sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Regarding data standards, less than a quarter of survey respondents (= 18; 23%) reported that the variables collected in their cohort corresponded to an internationally accepted standard.
findings.evidence: International online survey of 78 respondents from 62 AFI cohorts across 23 countries; barriers scored on sliders and classified with the PEARL framework.
findings.effect_size: 23% (18/78) used an international data standard; documented external-access process for 26% clin-epi, 19% samples, 4% genetic data
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Twenty (26%) respondents indicated that their cohort had a documented process for external groups to access clin-epi data, 15 (19%) for human biological samples, and 3 (4%) for human genetic data.
findings.study_system: acute febrile illness research cohorts (62 cohorts, 23 countries) survey

findings.claim: Health researchers overwhelmingly share data privately within their own project team, while public/repository deposition and reuse of others' public data are the least-practiced behaviors.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Results indicate that, on average, participants share their research data with other members in the same research project, with a mean score of 4.74, ranked first among all the statements.
findings.evidence: Questionnaire survey of 362 health scholars measuring data-sharing and reuse behaviors on Likert scales.
findings.effect_size: within-project sharing mean 4.74 (ranked first); 33.1% never reused publicly available data
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The majority of the participants (33.1%) reported never reusing publicly available data.
findings.study_system: health scholars survey, US university

findings.claim: In a survey of sub-Saharan African health-research networks, most researchers reported sharing datasets, but only about a quarter used institutional data repositories, with infrastructure, platform, policy and skills gaps limiting sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Furthermore, most respondents shared their research datasets and research outputs through institutional data repositories (42/160, 26.1%), scientific conferences (123/160, 76.9%), and journal articles (110/160, 68.8%).
findings.evidence: Cross-sectional mixed-methods web survey of 160 researchers/support staff across three SSA health-innovation networks and Global-North affiliates.
findings.effect_size: 63.8% (102/160) shared datasets; only 26.1% (42/160) via institutional data repositories
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: More than half of the respondents shared their research datasets (102/160, 63.8%), and 61.3% (98/160) shared research findings with the research community through different channels.
findings.study_system: health researchers in sub-Saharan Africa (3 research networks) survey

findings.claim: Australian health data custodians identify legislative hurdles, lack of uniform data-access standards, and inconsistent consent protocols as key barriers to sharing health data for research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The study highlighted several common challenges affecting data sharing for research, including legislative hurdles, lack of uniform standards for data access, and inconsistent consent protocols across datasets.
findings.evidence: Qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 11 data custodians across nine Australian healthcare organisations.
findings.study_system: Australian health data custodians (qualitative interviews)

findings.claim: Interviews with global-health data actors found that mandated data sharing rarely delivers impact because shared data are seldom analysis-ready (incomplete metadata, under-resourced curation) and academic reuse is driven by publication potential rather than health impact.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Secondary data users reported that shared data were seldom ready for analysis owing to incomplete metadata and under-resourced data curation.
findings.evidence: Thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 22 key informants (researchers, policy makers, funders, pharma) experienced in using clinical research data.
findings.study_system: global health clinical-data reuse (qualitative interviews)

findings.claim: A FAIR-compliant imaging-biomarker catalog was developed with a unified descriptor set across five domains to standardize discovery, comparison and reuse of imaging biomarkers across research, regulatory and clinical settings.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A unified biomarker descriptor set was established across five domains: core identification (imaging biomarker name, surrogation, clinical relevance), clinical context (main target, organ(s), disease/substrate, range(s), actionability), imaging and technical information (image modality, acquisition technique, technical parameters, extraction, association type, dimensionality, units), validation (robustness and use endorsed by publications, endorsed by professional societies, regulatory qualifications), and administrative data (repository, version/author).
findings.evidence: Three-phase consensus review of FDA-NIH BEST, QIBA, EMA, ESR-EIBALL resources; attributes extracted, deduplicated by expert consensus, organized into FAIR-aligned domains and tested on ADC, FDG-PET, radiomics and Doppler indices.
findings.effect_size: unified descriptor set across five domains
findings.study_system: imaging biomarkers metadata catalog (radiology)

findings.claim: The NIAID Data Ecosystem Discovery Portal harmonizes metadata from domain-specific and generalist repositories into a unified search interface over 4 million infectious/immune-disease datasets to improve findability, accessibility and reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Data Ecosystem Discovery Portal (https://data.niaid.nih.gov) provides a unified search interface for over 4 million data sets relevant to infectious and immune-mediated disease (IID) research.
findings.evidence: Resource report describing metadata harmonization across repositories with filters, prebuilt queries and an API for programmatic access.
findings.effect_size: over 4 million datasets indexed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Data Ecosystem Discovery Portal (https://data.niaid.nih.gov) provides a unified search interface for over 4 million data sets relevant to infectious and immune-mediated disease (IID) research.
findings.study_system: infectious/immune disease dataset discovery portal (metadata harmonization)

findings.claim: A cross-disciplinary interview study of 60 researchers found reproducibility (including data and research-material sharing) is a socially and institutionally mediated activity dependent on incentives, infrastructure and resourcing, not an individual choice.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Researchers described reproducibility as less of an individual choice but as a socially and institutionally mediated activity, dependent on enabling conditions such as supportive policies, adequate infrastructure, and equitable resource distribution.
findings.evidence: Framework analysis of semi-structured interviews with 60 researchers across the EU and UK, sampled for disciplinary, career-stage, gender and geographic diversity.
findings.study_system: cross-disciplinary researchers EU/UK (qualitative interviews on reproducibility)

findings.claim: In a simulation replacing concurrent controls with virtual control groups across 40 Wistar Han rat studies, VCGs reproduced effect-size decisions on liver enzymes with >=90% agreement in 68.5% of comparisons, and hybrid VCGs (keeping 50% real controls) raised full agreement from 46.9% to 76.7%.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In 68.5% of all the pairwise comparisons performed there was at least 90% agreement in effect size estimate between analysis done with CCG and VCGs.
findings.evidence: Results/Section 3.6: quantifies concordance of virtual vs concurrent controls and improvement with hybrid design.
findings.effect_size: at least 90% agreement in 68.5% of comparisons; full agreement rose from 46.9% (full VCG) to 76.7% (hybrid VCG); full disagreement fell from 2.6% to 0.15%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Specifically, full agreement based on effect size increased significantly (from 46.9% to 76.7%), and full disagreement dropped to near-zero (from 2.6% to 0.15%).
findings.study_system: Wistar Han rat toxicity studies; liver enzymes ALT/ALP/AST; VCG vs concurrent control simulation

findings.claim: In the largest curated multi-company control database (457,605 data points from 1,288 Han Wistar rat studies), study year was the most influential covariate on clinical laboratory parameters, exceeding company and body-weight class effects, implying temporal drift in historical control data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In both sexes, the study year emerged as the most important factor with a medium effect (mean effect size: 0.127 for females, 0.117 for males), followed by company (0.097 for females, 0.102 for males) and body weight class (small effect: 0.047 for females, medium effect: 0.089 in males).
findings.evidence: Results/Discussion: partial eta squared analysis of covariates on control-group lab parameters.
findings.effect_size: study year partial eta^2 mean 0.127 (F)/0.117 (M); company 0.097/0.102; body weight class 0.047/0.089
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In both sexes, the study year emerged as the most important factor with a medium effect (mean effect size: 0.127 for females, 0.117 for males), followed by company (0.097 for females, 0.102 for males) and body weight class (small effect: 0.047 for females, medium effect: 0.089 in males).
findings.study_system: Han Wistar rat control groups; 5 European pharmaceutical companies; ViCoG database

findings.claim: A case study identified anesthesia protocol (CO2 vs isoflurane, changed after 2017) as a hidden confounder that shifted control serum calcium means, showing how undocumented covariate drift undermines historical-control-derived VCGs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Before 2017, the mean values of calcium in serum were at (2.87 ± 0.14) mmol/L (95% CI [2.85, 2.90]) and dropped afterwards to (2.55 ± 0.07) mmol/L (95% CI [2.53, 2.56]).
findings.evidence: Results: anesthesia-driven confounding of control electrolyte values in HCD.
findings.effect_size: serum calcium 2.87±0.14 mmol/L (pre-2017) vs 2.55±0.07 mmol/L (post-2017); 95% CI of difference [0.31, 0.37], p<2.2e-16
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For calcium, the 95% CI for the difference in means resulted in [0.31, 0.37] with a-value of <2.2 e−16.
findings.study_system: male Wistar rats; serum calcium; legacy toxicity study; VCG feasibility

findings.claim: An external control arm built from real-world data failed to reproduce a lung-cancer RCT hazard ratio (ECA HR 1.53 vs RCT 0.91), but Bayesian borrowing from a historical control trial pulled the estimate toward the RCT value and improved precision.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The Cox HR estimates for the TTA versus ECA are consistently higher than the gold standard RCT HR estimate of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.73–1.13; p = 0.39) () in the CM subpopulation, indicating that the ECA analysis was unsuccessful at replicating the results of the RCT.
findings.evidence: Results: external control arm vs RCT benchmark and Bayesian borrowing sensitivity.
findings.effect_size: ECA HR 1.53 (95% CI 1.21-1.93) vs RCT HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.73-1.13); Bayesian borrowing reduced HR from 1.669 to 1.295 as weight went 0->1
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Forest plots summarizing the results of the four BB scenarios show that as borrowing weights increase from 0 to 1, the HR decreases from 1.669 (95% CrI: 1.328–2.103) to 1.295 (95% CrI: 1.082–1.537) (A).
findings.study_system: first-line metastatic NSCLC patients (human); RWD external control + historical control trial

findings.claim: A Bayesian dynamic-borrowing group-sequential design for medical-device trials reduced required enrollment relative to a frequentist design while maintaining Type I error and power, borrowing from four heterogeneous historical control studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The sample size required to reach at least 80% of Power and to control the T1E rate under 5%, using a frequentist one-stage design, was 2,282.
findings.evidence: Results/Discussion: sample-size reduction via Bayesian dynamic borrowing under congruence.
findings.effect_size: frequentist one-stage n=2,282; GSD max n=2,386; congruent scenarios enrolled ~1,497 vs 2,386; historical heterogeneity I^2=92%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The proposed design, when evaluated under scenarios where historical and current data were congruent (scenarios 1 and 2), demonstrated a significant reduction in the number of enrolled patients (1,497 vs. 2,386 under H​ and 1,850 vs. 2,386 under H​) while maintaining both the T1E and Power at their nominal levels.
findings.study_system: cardiovascular medical device trial (human); 4 historical control studies; SAM prior

findings.claim: A review of two proof-of-concept VCG studies found substantial non-reproducibility of quantitative endpoints, especially clinical pathology, when concurrent controls were replaced with virtual ones: 31%, 40% and 49% of parameters in three legacy studies became statistically non-reproducible.
findings.claim_source_sentence: When the CCG was replaced with VCG, the result showed that 31% (34 of 108 parameters), 40% (43 out of 107 parameters), and 49% (57 of 115 parameters) of the quantitative parameters were not statistically reproducible in the legacy studies A, B and C respectively ().
findings.evidence: Findings section: quantifies non-reproducibility of clinical pathology parameters under VCG replacement; notes NOAEL unchanged.
findings.effect_size: 31% (34/108), 40% (43/107), 49% (57/115) of quantitative parameters non-reproducible across three legacy studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: When the CCG was replaced with VCG, the result showed that 31% (34 of 108 parameters), 40% (43 out of 107 parameters), and 49% (57 of 115 parameters) of the quantitative parameters were not statistically reproducible in the legacy studies A, B and C respectively ().
findings.study_system: rat toxicity legacy studies; clinical pathology; VCG vs concurrent control

findings.claim: The Ramazzini Institute Global Glyphosate Study interpreted treated-group tumor increases against its own and NTP historical control databases, reporting leukemia at 1.63% vs 0.90% in 1,670 pooled historical controls.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The historical controls of the RI include 7142 animals (3572 males and 3570 females) from studies performed between 1984 and 2008, while NTP historical controls include 1180 animal (590 females and 590 males) from studies performed between 2011 and 2019.
findings.evidence: Methods/Results: use of historical control incidences to contextualize rare-tumor findings in a contested bioassay.
findings.effect_size: leukemia incidence 1.63% (current study) vs 0.90% in 1,670 pooled historical controls (15/1670)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In 1670 historical controls, only 15 animals were diagnosed with leukemia with an overall incidence rate of 0.90% in comparison to 1.63% of the current study.
findings.study_system: Sprague-Dawley rats; lifetime carcinogenicity; RI and NTP historical control databases

findings.claim: EFSA rejected a Ramazzini Institute carcinogenicity study's conclusions in part because its historical control data were from 1973-1983 (decades before the study) and it lacked an appropriate concurrent control and recent historical database.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The Panel noted that the data made available by the Ramazzini Institute as regards historical control data for neoplastic lesions were for the period 1973 up to 1983.
findings.evidence: Assessment: critique of outdated/inadequate historical controls and absence of proximate concurrent controls.
findings.effect_size: control-male haematopoietic neoplasia incidence 7.7% within old historical range 0-12.5%; low vs 15.7% in CD-1 mice at 104 weeks
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The incidence of lymphomas and leukaemias in control males (7.7%) was within the normal range for these tumours observed in (very old) historical control mice (0–12.5%) in the Ramazzini Institute but rather low in comparison with the incidence of haematopoietic neoplasias in CD‐1 mice at 104 weeks of age (15.7%) (Charles River Laboratories,; Bradley et al.,).
findings.study_system: Swiss mice carcinogenicity (sucralose); regulatory re-evaluation of historical control adequacy

findings.claim: The seminal proposal to introduce virtual control groups into preclinical toxicology argued that a repository of historical animal control-group data could be used to construct VCGs for toxicity studies, with a stated potential of about 25% reduction in animal use.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Historical animal control group data may lead to a repository, which could be used to construct virtual control groups (VCGs) for toxicity studies.
findings.evidence: Abstract: introduces the VCG concept; also states the ~25% reduction estimate (corroborated by altex.2403141 and 01926233241300310).
findings.study_system: regulatory animal toxicity studies (concept paper)

findings.claim: VCGs created from historical control data can cut the number of concurrent control animals in regulatory toxicity studies by up to 25%, with initial body weight (a surrogate for age) shown to be a critical matching variable.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Virtual control groups (VCGs) created from historical control data (HCD) can reduce the number of concurrent control group animals needed in regulatory toxicity studies by up to 25%.
findings.evidence: Abstract: reduction estimate and role of body-weight selection.
findings.effect_size: up to 25% reduction in concurrent control animals
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Virtual control groups (VCGs) created from historical control data (HCD) can reduce the number of concurrent control group animals needed in regulatory toxicity studies by up to 25%.
findings.study_system: 28-day rodent toxicity studies; body-weight matching for VCG sampling

findings.claim: A retrospective analysis of the eTOX database found that VCGs best reproduced original toxicologist designations of treatment-relatedness for histopathological findings when matched at the highest covariate similarity (same species, strain, sex, route and vehicle).
findings.claim_source_sentence: Generally, the best agreement was achieved when CCGs were replaced with VCGs with the highest level of similarity; the same species, strain, sex, administration route, and vehicle.
findings.evidence: Abstract: covariate-similarity governs VCG-CCG agreement on histopathology.
findings.effect_size: 28 selected histopathological findings analyzed in rat and dog
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: As a case study we retrospectively analyzed the impact of replacing Concurrent Control Groups (CCGs) with VCGs on the treatment-relatedness of 28 selected histopathological findings reported in either rat or dog in the eTOX database.
findings.study_system: rat and dog; eTOX database; histopathological findings

findings.claim: Using three four-week rat oral toxicity legacy studies as benchmarks, a framework evaluated whether VCGs could reproduce statistically significant deviations, test-substance-related effects, and overall study conclusions when replacing concurrent controls.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Replacing concurrent controls of legacy studies with VCGs should ideally reproduce the results of these studies.
findings.evidence: Abstract: multi-level VCG performance evaluation concept.
findings.study_system: rat oral toxicity (4-week) legacy studies; VCG performance benchmarking

findings.claim: A workshop concluded that historical control data could be repurposed into virtual control groups to partly or entirely replace concurrent controls, but that data curation, statistical evaluation and a validation strategy are prerequisites before implementation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Due to the highly controlled environment in which the studies are performed and the homogeneity of the animal collectives it has been proposed to use the historical data to build so-called virtual control groups, which could partly or entirely replace the concurrent control group.
findings.evidence: Abstract: prerequisites for regulatory implementation of VCGs.
findings.study_system: regulatory animal safety studies; VCG implementation prerequisites

findings.claim: The Innovative Health Initiative project VICT3R was launched to build a standardized annotated control-animal database and computational tools, with the explicit aim of obtaining regulatory acceptance for the virtual control group concept.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The new Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) project VICT3R aims to address these challenges and to obtain regulatory acceptance for the VCG concept.
findings.evidence: Abstract: VICT3R consortium for VCG database and regulatory acceptance.
findings.study_system: cross-company control-animal database; toxicology; 3Rs reduction initiative

findings.claim: VCGs were proposed in 2020 to reduce animal use while integrating historical control data, and laboratories running harmonized developmental and reproductive toxicity studies are encouraged to begin planning VCG implementation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The use of virtual control groups (VCGs) in nonclinical toxicology studies was first proposed in 2020 with the main purpose of reducing animal use while integrating historical control data (HCD) to enhance study interpretation.
findings.evidence: Abstract: perspectives on VCG in DART studies.
findings.study_system: rodent and rabbit developmental and reproductive toxicity (DART) studies

findings.claim: A proof-of-concept rat study using a Genentech historical control database identified sex, route of administration, fasting status and body weight at study initiation as key criteria for matching virtual to concurrent controls.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Sex, route of administration, fasting status, and body weight at study initiation were among the parameters that were indicated as key matching criteria.
findings.evidence: Abstract: key matching criteria and sources of control variability.
findings.study_system: Sprague-Dawley rat toxicity studies; Genentech historical control database

findings.claim: Recognizing NHP shortages and 3Rs pressures, a Scientific and Regulatory Policy Committee proposal recommends approaches to significantly reduce the number of control nonhuman primates euthanized in nonclinical toxicity studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Given the practical and ethical limitations on availability and/or use of NHPs and in line with the widely accepted guiding "3Rs" (replace, reduce, and refine) principles, many approaches have been considered to optimize toxicity study designs to meaningfully reduce the number of NHPs used.
findings.evidence: Abstract: reducing control NHP use, a driver for control-data reuse strategies.
findings.study_system: nonhuman primates; nonclinical toxicity study design; control-group reduction

findings.claim: A tutorial frames statisticians' partnership with Institutional Animal Care and Use Committees around the 3Rs, including emerging reduction strategies such as reuse of control data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We review the "3Rs" principles (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement) which are the foundation for the humane use of animals in scientific research, and how statisticians can partner with IACUC to help ensure robust and reproducible research while adhering to the 3Rs principles.
findings.evidence: Abstract: statistical stewardship of 3Rs reduction including control-data reuse.
findings.study_system: animal research statistics; IACUC; 3Rs reduction

findings.claim: Applying VCG data retrospectively to 20 pilot studies, the analysis reported that VCGs maintained toxicological statistical power and biological relevance while reducing animal usage, in the context of the FDA Modernization Act 2.0.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We applied VCG data retrospectively to 20 pilot studies.
findings.evidence: Abstract: 20-study re-analysis of VCG statistical and biological alignment.
findings.effect_size: 20 pilot studies re-analyzed with VCG data
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We applied VCG data retrospectively to 20 pilot studies.
findings.study_system: nonclinical pilot studies; VCG vs concurrent control re-analysis

findings.claim: The IMI eTOX consortium built the largest preclinical toxicity database, but identifies the unwillingness to share proprietary data and lack of published data sets as the biggest hurdle to establishing preclinical safety databases for pharmaceutical compounds.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Whereas toxicity data collection and sharing is now common practice for chemicals falling under the European REACH regulation (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals), the biggest hurdle for establishing preclinical safety databases for pharmaceutical compounds is the unwillingness to share proprietary data and lack of published data sets.
findings.evidence: Abstract: data-sharing barriers underlying the ethical-debt / control-data-reuse problem.
findings.study_system: shared preclinical toxicity database (eTOX); 13 pharmaceutical companies

findings.claim: A review on historical control data in rodent carcinogenicity bioassays stresses that HCD should never be used in isolation to dismiss an apparent treatment-related tumor increase or supersede a weight-of-evidence evaluation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: It is emphasized throughout the review that HCD should not be used in isolation to dismiss an apparent treatment-related increased tumor incidence and should never supersede a detailed "weight of evidence" evaluation in coming to any conclusion as to the result of a carcinogenicity bioassay.
findings.evidence: Abstract: cautions on regulatory use of HCD in carcinogenicity interpretation.
findings.study_system: rodent lifetime carcinogenicity bioassays; historical control databases

findings.claim: A laboratory conducted a 26-week Tg.rasH2 carcinogenicity study specifically to generate a historical control database for mice sourced from CLEA Japan, addressing a gap in published spontaneous-tumor incidence data for this source.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We conducted a 26-week carcinogenicity study at our test facility on Tg.rasH2 mice sourced from CLEA Japan Inc., in a process to generate historical control database.
findings.evidence: Abstract: source-specific HCD generation for a validated bioassay model.
findings.study_system: Tg.rasH2 mice (CLEA Japan); 26-week carcinogenicity; HCD generation

findings.claim: A Labcorp historical control database of ~3,600 Sprague-Dawley rats from 104-week studies documented background neoplasm incidences, with pituitary adenoma the most prevalent benign tumor (56.4% males, 77.1% females).
findings.claim_source_sentence: Data collected from approximately 1800 male and 1800 female Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats used in 104-week carcinogenicity studies were archived in a historical control database at Labcorp Early Development, Inc, and the neoplastic microscopic observation data from these rats were retrospectively evaluated.
findings.evidence: Abstract: background neoplasm incidence reference from a commercial HCD.
findings.effect_size: pituitary adenoma pars distalis 56.4% (M) / 77.1% (F); mammary carcinoma 25% (F)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Pituitary adenoma of pars distalis was found to be the most prevalent benign neoplasm in both males and females (56.4% and 77.1%).
findings.study_system: Sprague-Dawley rats; 104-week carcinogenicity; historical control database

findings.claim: In control Tg.rasH2 mice across nine 26-week studies at two CROs, spontaneous subcapsular adrenal hyperplasia was very common (56-79% males, 88-100% females), illustrating high non-neoplastic background variability that HCD must capture.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Incidence of this finding ranged from 56% to 79% in males and 88% to 100% in females, with an incidence average of 62% in males and 93% in females.
findings.evidence: Abstract: high background lesion incidence in control transgenic mice.
findings.effect_size: adrenal subcapsular hyperplasia 56-79% (M, avg 62%); 88-100% (F, avg 93%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Incidence of this finding ranged from 56% to 79% in males and 88% to 100% in females, with an incidence average of 62% in males and 93% in females.
findings.study_system: control Tg.rasH2 mice; nine 26-week carcinogenicity studies; two CROs

findings.claim: A historical control database of 1,420 Tg.rasH2 mice across 26 studies reported low, stable spontaneous tumor incidences (lung adenoma 10.14% M / 5.77% F), supporting the model's use as a shorter, lower-animal-number carcinogenicity assay.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The most common spontaneous tumors in the Tg.rasH2 mice were alveolar bronchiolar adenoma of the lungs (10.14% in males and 5.77% in females) and hemangiosarcoma of the spleen (3.66% in both males and females).
findings.evidence: Abstract: HCD of spontaneous tumor incidence in a validated short-term bioassay.
findings.effect_size: lung alveolar bronchiolar adenoma 10.14% (M) / 5.77% (F); splenic hemangiosarcoma 3.66%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The most common spontaneous tumors in the Tg.rasH2 mice were alveolar bronchiolar adenoma of the lungs (10.14% in males and 5.77% in females) and hemangiosarcoma of the spleen (3.66% in both males and females).
findings.study_system: Tg.rasH2 mice; 26 studies; historical control database

findings.claim: A comparison of internal and published rasH2 mouse data found remarkably similar spontaneous tumor incidences across studies over a decade (lung adenoma mean 3.9-9.9%), indicating minimal drift in the model and supporting reliable historical control data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The remarkable similarity in the tumor incidences in multiple rasH2 studies over a decade and the observed stability of the inserted human gene are important indicators of the minimal drift in this model.
findings.evidence: Abstract: minimal drift supports reliability of historical control incidences.
findings.effect_size: lung bronchiolo-alveolar adenoma mean 3.9-9.9% (range 0-18%); splenic hemangiosarcoma mean 3.0-3.9% (range 0-17%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Incidences of common spontaneous tumors (incidences > 1%) observed in these studies were lung bronchiolo-alveolar adenomas (mean 3.9-9.9%; range 0-18%), lung bronchiolo-alveolar adenocarcinomas (mean 1.4-2.4%; range 0-5%), splenic hemangiosarcomas (mean 3.0-3.9%; range 0-17%), cutaneous squamous cell papillomas (mean 1.1-1.2%; range 0-4%), Harderian gland adenoma (mean 0.8-1.2%; range 0-4%), and hepatocellular adenomas (mean 1.8%; 0-9% in males only).
findings.study_system: rasH2 mice; 6-month carcinogenicity; cross-study HCD comparison

findings.claim: Analysis of the RITA shared industry historical control database showed that spontaneous Leydig cell adenoma incidence in control rats is strongly strain-dependent (near 100% in F344, 4.2% in Sprague-Dawley, 13.7% in Wistar) and further modulated by breeder, diet and age.
findings.claim_source_sentence: High incidences of close to 100% have been found in F344 rats, while the mean incidence was 4.2% in Sprague-Dawley rats and 13.7% in Wistar rats.
findings.evidence: Abstract: strain/breeder dependence of control tumor incidence in a shared HCD.
findings.effect_size: Leydig cell adenoma incidence ~100% (F344), 4.2% (Sprague-Dawley), 13.7% (Wistar)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: High incidences of close to 100% have been found in F344 rats, while the mean incidence was 4.2% in Sprague-Dawley rats and 13.7% in Wistar rats.
findings.study_system: rats (F344, Sprague-Dawley, Wistar); RITA historical control database; Leydig cell tumors

findings.claim: A new Bayesian dynamic-borrowing method (synthetic prior with covariates, SPx) borrows information from historical trials using only trial-level summaries and can substantially reduce the required control group size while preserving frequentist operating characteristics.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Through simulations and an application to the rheumatoid arthritis trial we show that SPx can substantially reduce the control group size while maintaining Frequentist properties.
findings.evidence: Abstract: control-size reduction via covariate-adjusted Bayesian borrowing.
findings.study_system: rheumatoid arthritis clinical trial (human); dynamic borrowing of historical controls

findings.claim: A prospectively specified adaptive Bayesian borrowing method borrows from historical control data in proportion to observed congruence with current data, increasing control-arm precision while mitigating prior-data conflict.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A novel adaptive Bayesian borrowing (ABB) method proposed here borrows from historical control data to increase the precision of the control arm based on the observed congruence of the historical and current data.
findings.evidence: Abstract: congruence-based adaptive borrowing to reduce control burden.
findings.study_system: clinical trials (rare/pediatric diseases); adaptive borrowing of historical controls

findings.claim: The BEAM hybrid design integrates historical controls and real-world data via multisource exchangeability modeling with adaptive sample size, controlling Type I error and reducing bias when heterogeneity exists between current and historical data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Through extensive simulations, BEAM demonstrated robust performance in controlling type I error rate, reducing bias, and maintaining power compared to traditional methods and other adaptive designs.
findings.evidence: Abstract: adaptive hybrid borrowing controlling type I error under heterogeneity.
findings.study_system: ankylosing spondylitis case study (human); hybrid trial with historical controls

findings.claim: A Bayesian hybrid design uses a dynamic power prior to borrow from a completed historical monotherapy study, enhancing power of otherwise uncontrolled single-arm oncology trials with explicit, tunable borrowing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Compared to traditional single-arm designs, the hybrid design may significantly enhance power by borrowing external information, enabling a more robust assessment of activity.
findings.evidence: Abstract: dynamic power prior borrowing from historical control.
findings.study_system: early-phase oncology combination trials (human); dynamic power prior; nonconcurrent control

findings.claim: The latent exchangeability prior (LEAP) improves on blanket-discounting priors (power, commensurate, robust MAP) by classifying historical subjects into exchangeable and non-exchangeable groups and borrowing only from the most relevant ones.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The LEAP discounts the historical data by identifying the most relevant subjects from the historical data.
findings.evidence: Abstract: selective (latent-exchangeability) borrowing from historical controls.
findings.study_system: phase 3 plaque psoriasis trial (human); latent exchangeability prior for control augmentation

findings.claim: Extending LEAP to time-to-event data, the authors caution that although borrowing among external controls can yield efficiency gains, operating characteristics can be poor when exchangeability fails, tempering enthusiasm for external-control borrowing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Simulation results suggest that, although efficiency gains can be achieved by borrowing information among external controls, operating characteristics in general can be quite poor under a lack of exchangeability.
findings.evidence: Abstract: caveat on external-control borrowing under non-exchangeability.
findings.study_system: second-line metastatic colorectal cancer trial (human); time-to-event external-control borrowing

findings.claim: A multi-source dynamic borrowing Bayesian framework quantifies heterogeneity between data sources and discounts each separately without assuming exchangeability, outperforming existing methods on power and mean squared error under heterogeneity and baseline imbalance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our approach outperformed existing methods by enhancing power and reducing MSE, while effectively controlling type I error and bias in the presence of heterogeneity and baseline imbalances.
findings.evidence: Abstract: heterogeneity-aware multi-source borrowing from historical/real-world controls.
findings.study_system: relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma application (human); multi-source dynamic borrowing

findings.claim: A dynamic power prior for non-inferiority trials with normal endpoints discounts borrowing from historical control data as a function of the Hellinger distance between historical and current control posteriors.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Specifically, we consider a dynamic power prior that possibly allows to discount the level of borrowing in the presence of heterogeneity between past and current control data.
findings.evidence: Abstract: distance-based discounting of historical control borrowing.
findings.study_system: non-inferiority trials (human); dynamic power prior for historical active-control borrowing

findings.claim: A discussion of the LEAP method highlights two considerations for hybrid control arms: the necessity for extrapolation and the potential benefits of curating historical control data before analysis.
