findings.claim_source_sentence: We commend Alt et al.'s innovative approach for analysis with a hybrid control arm while offering insights into two key considerations: the necessity for extrapolation and the potential benefits of curating historical control data before analysis.
findings.evidence: Abstract: emphasizes curation of historical control data prior to borrowing.
findings.study_system: commentary on hybrid control-arm borrowing methodology (human trials)

findings.claim: In a 2-year rat inhalation carcinogenicity study of nano-titanium dioxide, an observed bronchiolo-alveolar carcinoma increase was judged non-adverse because the incidence sat at the upper limit of the JBRC historical control database, exemplifying HCD-based dismissal of a marginal finding.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, this incidence was at the upper limit of JBRC's historical control data.
findings.evidence: Abstract: use of HCD upper limit to interpret a marginal tumor increase.
findings.study_system: F344 rats; 2-year inhalation carcinogenicity; JBRC historical control data

findings.claim: The RITA shared historical control database standardises tissue sampling, harmonised nomenclature and peer review, and by ~2002 held 10,896 rats from 106 studies with over 17,604 primary tumours to contextualise rare or marginal tumour findings.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the RITA database, there are currently 10,896 rats from 106 studies with more than 17,604 primary tumors and 16,551 pre-neoplastic lesions.
findings.evidence: Abstract: scale and standardisation of a shared industry historical control tumour database.
findings.effect_size: 10,896 rats; 106 studies; 17,604 primary tumours; 16,551 pre-neoplastic lesions
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In the RITA database, there are currently 10,896 rats from 106 studies with more than 17,604 primary tumors and 16,551 pre-neoplastic lesions.
findings.study_system: rats (Wistar, Sprague-Dawley) and mice; RITA shared historical control database

findings.claim: The North American Control Animal Database (NACAD) was established in 1994 by ILSI-affiliated companies, modelled on RITA, to pool neoplastic and proliferative control-animal lesions using standardised nomenclature and diagnostic criteria for cross-study comparison.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Utilizing the model established by RITA and working with the International Life Sciences Institute (ILSI), companies with laboratories in North America formed a working group in 1994 to establish and maintain a database of neoplastic and proliferative lesions from control animals in carcinogenicity studies.
findings.evidence: Abstract: founding of a shared North American control-animal database on standardised nomenclature.
findings.study_system: rat and mouse control animals; North American Control Animal Database (NACAD)

findings.claim: The IMI eTRANSAFE ToxHub integrated ~6,500 preclinical studies from the earlier eTOX project and began collecting standardised control data from oral 4-week repeat-dose rat studies across five companies, building the shared legacy-data infrastructure underpinning virtual control groups.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Further in vivo animal toxicology study data have been made available through the integration of 6500 preclinical studies from the eTOX project [] into the eTRANSAFE ToxHub System.
findings.evidence: Results/In Vivo Animal Toxicology Study Data (fulltext body): scale of legacy preclinical data integrated for control-data reuse.
findings.effect_size: 6,500 eTOX studies integrated; control data from 5 companies (oral 4-week rat studies)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Further in vivo animal toxicology study data have been made available through the integration of 6500 preclinical studies from the eTOX project [] into the eTRANSAFE ToxHub System.
findings.study_system: preclinical toxicology studies; eTRANSAFE/eTOX shared database; 13 pharma companies

findings.claim: Using the sendigR R package to query FDA CDER SEND datasets, the background incidence of spontaneous liver necrosis in control rats rose from ~2% at ages matching 1-month studies to ~8% at ages matching 6-month terminal sacrifice, showing historical control background rates are strongly age/study-duration dependent.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The background incidence rate of liver necrosis was found to be higher, approximately 8%, in older rats at ages matching terminal sacrifice during 6-month studies.
findings.evidence: Results (fulltext body): age-dependence of control background lesion incidence extracted from a SEND cross-study database.
findings.effect_size: liver necrosis background ~2% (1-month) rising to ~8% (6-month terminal-sacrifice ages)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The background incidence rate of liver necrosis was found to be higher, approximately 8%, in older rats at ages matching terminal sacrifice during 6-month studies.
findings.study_system: control rats; CDISC SEND datasets (FDA CDER); sendigR cross-study analysis

findings.claim: An FDA-requested Tumor Combination Guide maps INHAND tumour nomenclature to the SEND NEOPLASM controlled terminology so tumour types can be combined consistently for statistical analysis of rodent carcinogenicity data across studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This guide provides a higher-level hierarchy of tumor types or categories correlating the tumor names from the International Harmonization of Nomenclature and Diagnostic Criteria (INHAND) publications with those available in the NEOPLASM controlled terminology (CT) code list in SEND.
findings.evidence: Abstract: harmonising INHAND and SEND terminology for cross-study tumour data analysis.
findings.study_system: rodent carcinogenicity tumour data; INHAND-to-SEND terminology mapping

findings.claim: A Toxicologic Pathology Forum opinion notes the INHAND initiative has established globally accepted lesion terminology for laboratory species but identifies gaps requiring new diagnostic nomenclature for medical-device studies, underscoring that standardised control-lesion terminology is still incomplete.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The International Harmonization of Nomenclature and Diagnostic Criteria for Lesions (INHAND) initiative has established globally accepted terminology for proliferative and nonproliferative lesions in various laboratory animal species.
findings.evidence: Abstract: status and gaps of INHAND standardised lesion nomenclature.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal lesions; medical devices; INHAND nomenclature

findings.claim: The INHAND project published standardized nomenclature for proliferative and nonproliferative lesions of ocular tissues in nonrodent species (rabbits, dogs, minipigs, nonhuman primates), a prerequisite for pooling background control-lesion data across laboratories and countries.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The purpose of this publication is to provide a standardized nomenclature for classifying lesions observed in ocular tissues (eyes and glands and ocular adnexa) from laboratory nonrodent species (rabbits, dogs, minipigs, and nonhuman primates) used in nonclinical safety studies with an emphasis on ocular-targeted dosing.
findings.evidence: Abstract: harmonised nonrodent ocular lesion nomenclature enabling cross-lab control data comparison.
findings.study_system: nonrodent species (rabbit, dog, minipig, NHP); ocular tissues; INHAND nomenclature

findings.claim: A retrospective analysis of 15 intravitreal biotherapeutic programs found chronic ocular studies revealed no new clinically relevant toxicities beyond shorter studies, supporting reduction or removal of recovery groups and omission of chronic/systemic studies to cut animal use.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A retrospective analysis of 15 intravitreal biotherapeutic programs was conducted to identify strategies for reducing animal use in ocular drug development.
findings.evidence: Abstract: retrospective program review supporting recovery-group and study reduction.
findings.effect_size: 15 intravitreal biotherapeutic programs analysed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A retrospective analysis of 15 intravitreal biotherapeutic programs was conducted to identify strategies for reducing animal use in ocular drug development.
findings.study_system: ocular biotherapeutics; intravitreal repeat-dose toxicity programs

findings.claim: In a 111-mAb industry dataset, chronic (>=6-month) monoclonal-antibody toxicity studies revealed no new toxicities of human concern for over 85% (96/111) of molecules, and a weight-of-evidence model correctly advised the development strategy for 90% of mAbs, supporting shorter studies and reduced animal use.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For over 85% (96/111) of standard/modified mAbs, studies ≥ 6-months did not reveal any new toxicities of human concern, and for 71% of mAbs, no toxicities or no new toxicities were noted in chronic studies compared to FIH-enabling study findings.
findings.evidence: Results (fulltext body): quantified low incremental value of chronic mAb studies supporting 3Rs reduction.
findings.effect_size: 85% (96/111) of mAbs: no new toxicities of human concern in >=6-month studies; model correct for 90% of mAbs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For over 85% (96/111) of standard/modified mAbs, studies ≥ 6-months did not reveal any new toxicities of human concern, and for 71% of mAbs, no toxicities or no new toxicities were noted in chronic studies compared to FIH-enabling study findings.
findings.study_system: monoclonal antibodies; chronic toxicity study designs; MEB/NC3Rs survey

findings.claim: A cross-company review of monoclonal-antibody safety studies found recovery animals were included in 68% of first-in-human-enabling and 69% of later-development studies, often redundantly, identifying scope to reduce recovery-animal use by limiting inclusion to a single study and species.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Recovery animals were included in 68% of FIH-enabling and 69% of later-development studies, often in multiple studies in the same program.
findings.evidence: Abstract: prevalence of recovery-animal inclusion and reduction opportunity.
findings.effect_size: recovery animals in 68% of FIH-enabling and 69% of later-development mAb studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Recovery animals were included in 68% of FIH-enabling and 69% of later-development studies, often in multiple studies in the same program.
findings.study_system: monoclonal antibodies; recovery animals; NC3Rs/EPAA/MEB + 14 companies

findings.claim: A 30-organisation cross-company data-sharing initiative pooled 259 studies covering 137 compounds and found wide, often unjustified variation in recovery-animal inclusion, concluding recovery-animal use can be reduced without impacting drug development.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Data on 137 compounds (including 53 biologicals and 78 small molecules) from 259 studies showed wide variation in where, when and why recovery animals were included.
findings.evidence: Abstract: evidence base for reducing recovery-animal use via shared study-design data.
findings.effect_size: 137 compounds (53 biologicals, 78 small molecules); 259 studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Data on 137 compounds (including 53 biologicals and 78 small molecules) from 259 studies showed wide variation in where, when and why recovery animals were included.
findings.study_system: recovery animals; 30 organisations (pharma, CRO, academia, regulators)

findings.claim: A review of classical and new approaches to historical control data concludes their critical value in toxicological bioassays is realised only within a weight-of-evidence assessment, and proposes moving from binary inclusion/exclusion of HCD to a tiered, uncertainty-aware information contribution.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, the critical value of HCD in toxicological bioassays is highlighted when used in a weight-of-evidence assessment.
findings.evidence: Abstract: methodological framing of appropriate HCD use.
findings.study_system: regulatory toxicology bioassays; historical control data methodology

findings.claim: A proposed minimal metadata set (MNMS) to repurpose nonclinical in vivo data reports that the IMI eTRANSAFE project collected and analysed control and toxicology data from more than 60,000 rats, 1,300 dogs and 500 monkeys to enable virtual control groups.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The opportunities and challenges for implementing VCGs were the focus of the IMI eTRANSAFE project, which has collected and analyzed drug safety and toxicology data from more than 60,000 rats, 1,300 dogs and 500 monkeys (see ref.and more recently ref.).
findings.evidence: Introduction (fulltext body): scale of shared control-animal data available for VCGs and the metadata needed to reuse it.
findings.effect_size: >60,000 rats; 1,300 dogs; 500 monkeys (eTRANSAFE)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The opportunities and challenges for implementing VCGs were the focus of the IMI eTRANSAFE project, which has collected and analyzed drug safety and toxicology data from more than 60,000 rats, 1,300 dogs and 500 monkeys (see ref.and more recently ref.).
findings.study_system: nonclinical in vivo animal data; eTRANSAFE control database; FAIR metadata

findings.claim: A points-to-consider paper reports that partial replacement of concurrent controls by virtual controls in nonclinical safety studies has gained traction, being supported by foundational work, encouraged by regulators, and aligned with societal expectations on animal use.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The replacement of a proportion of concurrent controls by virtual controls in nonclinical safety studies has gained traction over the last few years.
findings.evidence: Abstract: momentum and considerations for partial VCG implementation.
findings.study_system: nonclinical safety studies; partial virtual-control replacement; database creation

findings.claim: A brief communication on reusing high-quality regulated control data for virtual control groups warns that despite evident ethical and cost benefits, VCGs must be systematically assessed to avoid lowering an animal study's sensitivity to detect adverse events, thresholds, target organs, or biomarkers.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While the ethical and cost-saving aspects of such a concept are immediately evident, the potential challenges need to be carefully considered to avoid any effect which could lower the sensitivity of an animal study to detect adverse events, safety thresholds, target organs, or biomarkers.
findings.evidence: Abstract: sensitivity-loss risk framing for VCG replacement of concurrent controls.
findings.study_system: regulated animal safety data; virtual control groups; sensitivity assessment

findings.claim: Re-analysing 20 (sub)chronic NHP toxicity studies with the concurrent control group omitted, 82% of statistically significant parameter differences were confirmed by a mixed-design ANOVA without concurrent controls, and all four dose-limiting toxicities were identifiable without reference to the concurrent control.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our investigation has demonstrated that out of 22 parameters with statistical difference in the fixed-effect ANOVA /Dunnett’s test, 82% could be confirmed using the mixed-design ANOVA.
findings.evidence: Results (fulltext body): concordance of findings when concurrent controls are omitted in NHP studies.
findings.effect_size: 82% (18/22) of significant parameters confirmed without concurrent control; 4/4 DLTs identifiable without control
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Our investigation has demonstrated that out of 22 parameters with statistical difference in the fixed-effect ANOVA /Dunnett’s test, 82% could be confirmed using the mixed-design ANOVA.
findings.study_system: non-human primates; (sub)chronic toxicity studies; concurrent vehicle control omission

findings.claim: Querying FDA CDER's repository of >1,800 SEND-format studies for a historical-control question, the frequency of data population across required fields ranged from 6% to 99%, and fields such as vehicle name, animal supplier and test facility were not amenable to accurate automated extraction without further SEND harmonisation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: FDA CDER's repository of >1800 sponsor-submitted studies in SEND format was queried using the statistical programming language R to gain insight into how the CDISC SEND Implementation Guides are being applied across the industry.
findings.evidence: Abstract: feasibility and limits of SEND-based cross-study historical control analysis.
findings.effect_size: field data-population frequency ranged from 6% to 99%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For each component needed to answer the question (defined as “query block”), the frequency of data population was determined and ranged from 6 to 99%.
findings.study_system: CDISC SEND datasets (FDA CDER); cross-study historical control extraction

findings.claim: A Toxicologic Pathology Forum opinion argues that validating virtual control groups requires running the VCG and the full concurrent control in parallel (dual study design) over varying durations, and that a validated VCG database must include digital histopathology slides for microscopic assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Ultimately, the most important step lies in the validation of the concept by performing VCG and the full control group in parallel for studies of varying duration over a reasonable timespan to confirm there are no differences in outcomes (dual study design).
findings.evidence: Abstract: proposed validation pathway for VCGs in anatomic pathology.
findings.study_system: nonclinical toxicity studies; anatomic pathology; VCG validation (dual study design)

findings.claim: A Japan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association paper states that replacing the concurrent control with a virtual control group reduces animal use by approximately 30%, but identifies five obstacles since current guidelines still mandate concurrent controls for pivotal studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Evaluating toxicology study results using historical control data is not new; however, introducing a VCG means replacing the concurrent control group in a toxicology study with a VCG, thereby reducing the number of animals used by approximately 30%.
findings.evidence: Abstract: industry perspective on ~30% reduction and regulatory barriers to VCGs.
findings.effect_size: ~30% reduction in animals used by replacing concurrent control with VCG
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Evaluating toxicology study results using historical control data is not new; however, introducing a VCG means replacing the concurrent control group in a toxicology study with a VCG, thereby reducing the number of animals used by approximately 30%.
findings.study_system: nonclinical toxicology studies; virtual control groups; Japanese industry/regulatory view

findings.claim: An EFSA Scientific Opinion proposes a stepwise quantitative decision scheme (seven steps in three clusters: planning, HCD evaluation, HCD use) to harmonise how historical control data are compiled and statistically integrated with concurrent control data for regulatory pesticide studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This Opinion proposes a stepwise, quantitative approach using a decision scheme which includes seven distinct steps grouped in three overall clusters of activity: (1) planning, (2) evaluation of the HCD and (3) use of HCD.
findings.evidence: Abstract: regulatory framework for quantitative HCD use and reporting.
findings.effect_size: seven-step decision scheme in three clusters
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This Opinion proposes a stepwise, quantitative approach using a decision scheme which includes seven distinct steps grouped in three overall clusters of activity: (1) planning, (2) evaluation of the HCD and (3) use of HCD.
findings.study_system: regulatory pesticide toxicity studies; historical control data; EFSA guidance

findings.claim: A review of methods for calculating historical control limits finds that although presenting HCD and validating the concurrent control against historical limits are now reporting requirements, many guidelines fail to define how limits should be calculated, leaving more issues open than solved after 40 years of discussion.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For reporting toxicology studies, the presentation of historical control data and the validation of the concurrent control group with respect to historical control limits have become requirements.
findings.evidence: Abstract: unresolved methodology of historical control limit calculation.
findings.study_system: toxicology studies (incl. genetic toxicology); historical control limits methodology

findings.claim: In a retrospective analysis of 22 nonrodent (dog and NHP) 1-month toxicity studies, virtual control groups matched by propensity score (body weight, age, study year) yielded similar or higher sensitivity than concurrent controls to detect test-article effects on body weight and clinical pathology when fold-change from baseline was used.
findings.claim_source_sentence: When the fold change from baseline was used, VCGs yielded a similar or higher statistical sensitivity to detect test article relatedness than CCGs.
findings.evidence: Abstract: first systematic VCG-vs-CCG statistical comparison in nonrodents.
findings.effect_size: 22 nonrodent studies; propensity-score matching by BW, age, year improved sensitivity
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Body weight and six clinical pathology endpoints were analyzed against the reported study findings from a cohort of 22 previously reported nonrodent 1-month oral gavage toxicity using three different methods of generating VCGs.
findings.study_system: dog and non-human primate; 1-month systemic toxicity studies; VCG vs CCG

findings.claim: A commentary on historical control data of rare events highlights five considerations (database size, rare-event handling, chronological patterns, point-estimate summaries, treatment independence), recommending exploratory analysis on as large an HCD database as possible to detect systemic bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The current commentary shortly highlights 5 points that should be considered when working with HCD of rare events: 1) HCD database (HCDB) size, 2) the issue of rare events, 3) potential chronological patterns, 4) using point estimates to summarize HCD and 5) independence from treatment bias, i.e., HCD are mostly informative for primary toxicity.
findings.evidence: Abstract: methodological cautions for HCD of rare events.
findings.effect_size: 5 considerations for HCD of rare events
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The current commentary shortly highlights 5 points that should be considered when working with HCD of rare events: 1) HCD database (HCDB) size, 2) the issue of rare events, 3) potential chronological patterns, 4) using point estimates to summarize HCD and 5) independence from treatment bias, i.e., HCD are mostly informative for primary toxicity.
findings.study_system: toxicological bioassays; historical control data of rare events

findings.claim: Using telemetry data from a 48-NHP moxifloxacin QTc study, same-laboratory historical controls could replace contemporary controls to detect a treatment's QTc effect (favouring group sizes >=18), but time-course differences between two laboratories' vehicle data meant cross-lab controls could not be used.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, differences in the time course of QTc effect in the vehicle data from the two laboratories meant that it was not possible to use cross-lab controls.
findings.evidence: Abstract: feasibility of same-lab but not cross-lab historical controls for QTc assessment.
findings.effect_size: n=48 NHP source study; same-lab historical controls usable, cross-lab not; advantage for group size >=18
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We used implanted telemetry data from a large nonhuman primate (NHP) cardiovascular study (n = 48) evaluating the effect of moxifloxacin.
findings.study_system: non-human primates; cardiovascular telemetry QTc; contemporary vs historical vs cross-lab controls

findings.claim: Evaluating JMPR pesticide assessments from 2004-2021, historical control data were used routinely and exclusively to avoid false-positive treatment-relatedness calls (mostly via the HCD extreme-value range), never to avoid false negatives or for quality control, and the assumption of a shared underlying distribution was not tested.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that HCD was used routinely and exclusively to avoid potential false positive decisions regarding the treatment-relatedness of effects, mostly using the HCD range, i.e., the most extreme values, as a benchmark.
findings.evidence: Abstract: documented one-sided regulatory use of HCD ranges.
findings.study_system: regulatory pesticide toxicology (JMPR 2004-2021); historical control data use

findings.claim: An IQ Consortium working-group survey of industry recovery-animal practice found case studies increasingly aligning with 2013 STP recommendations to exclude recovery cohorts by default, minimise recovery groups, and exclude recovery-phase control animals by leveraging external and dosing-phase data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The case studies presented in this paper demonstrate increasing alignment with the Society of Toxicologic Pathology recommendations (2013) towards (1) excluding recovery phase cohorts by default (include only when scientifically justified), (2) minimizing the number of recovery groups (e.g., control and one dose level), and (3) excluding controls in the recovery cohort by leveraging external and/or dosing phase data.
findings.evidence: Abstract: convergence toward reduced recovery (incl. recovery-control) animal use.
findings.study_system: repeat-dose toxicity studies; recovery animals; IQ Consortium survey

findings.claim: Analysing the eTOX shared database with likelihood ratios under matched exposure and duration, inter-species concordance of histopathological findings was rare; e.g., short-term liver-toxicity concordance between female rats and dogs had an average positive likelihood ratio of only 1.84 and negative LR of 0.73.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For example, liver toxicity concordance in short-term studies between female rats and dogs observed an average LR+ of 1.84, and an average LR- of 0.73.
findings.evidence: Abstract: low cross-species concordance limits reuse of one species' control/finding data for another.
findings.effect_size: liver toxicity female rat vs dog: mean LR+ 1.84, mean LR- 0.73; 24 new significant associations
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For example, liver toxicity concordance in short-term studies between female rats and dogs observed an average LR+ of 1.84, and an average LR- of 0.73.
findings.study_system: four preclinical species; eTOX database; inter-species histopathology concordance

findings.claim: A review of 3Rs endeavours by regulators, trade associations and industry notes that use of virtual controls, the value of the second toxicity species and information sharing are currently under scrutiny, but that companies and regulators resist abandoning current paradigms until replacement approaches are validated and globally accepted.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Use of virtual controls, value of the second toxicity species, information sharing and expectations for life-threatening diseases, human specific or well-characterised targets are currently being scrutinised.
findings.evidence: Abstract: positions VCGs and data sharing within the broader 3Rs regulatory landscape.
findings.study_system: regulatory toxicology; 3Rs initiatives; virtual controls and data sharing

findings.claim: The foundational meta-analytic-predictive (MAP) approach summarises historical control information via between-trial heterogeneity into a prior; e.g., 930 control patients across 11 historical Phase IV trials with small heterogeneity yielded a prior effective sample size of about 90 patients, bounded by the ratio of within- to between-trial variance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For a Phase IV trial (930 control patients in 11 historical trials) between-trial heterogeneity was fairly small, resulting in a prior effective sample size of approximately 90 patients.
findings.evidence: Abstract: seminal MAP-prior quantification of borrowable historical control information.

findings.claim: Extending the MAP approach to overdispersed count data, historical control lesion counts from nine multiple-sclerosis trials (1,936 control patients) with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity yielded a prior effective sample size of about 45 control patients, i.e., a Phase II control arm could be reduced by ~45 patients.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For the general population (without baseline enrichment), with 1936 control patients from nine historical trials, between-trial variability was moderate to substantial, leading to a prior effective sample size of about 45 control patients.
findings.evidence: Abstract: MAP borrowing quantified for count endpoints in MS trials.
findings.effect_size: 1,936 control patients (9 trials) -> prior ESS ~45 control patients

findings.claim: A study of prior effective sample size (ESS) methods shows existing information-based ESS measures fail a predictive-consistency criterion (expected posterior-predictive ESS should equal prior ESS plus N) and introduces a predictively consistent local-information-ratio ESS, relevant to quantifying how much a historical control prior is really worth.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We show that current methods fail a basic predictive consistency criterion, which requires the expected posterior-predictive ESS for a sample of size N to be the sum of the prior ESS and N.
findings.evidence: Abstract: corrects how borrowed historical control information is quantified.
findings.study_system: clinical trial priors (human); prior effective sample size for historical borrowing

findings.claim: A Bayesian semiparametric meta-analytic-predictive (BaSe-MAP) prior uses a Dirichlet process mixture to selectively borrow historical control information without prespecifying the amount of borrowing, adaptively learning the relationship between historical and current control data under heterogeneity or prior-data conflict.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To incorporate the ability to selectively borrow historic information, we propose a Bayesian semiparametric meta-analytic-predictive prior.
findings.evidence: Abstract: flexible selective borrowing extension of the MAP prior.
findings.study_system: phase II ankylosing spondylitis trial (human); semiparametric MAP prior

findings.claim: A methodological note links Pocock's original bias-variance model for historical controls (closely related to the commensurate prior) with the widely used robust mixture prior (RMP), showing different combinations of the RMP's weight and vague-component variance can express the same prior belief about how much historical data to borrow.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this note, we identify key features of the relationship between the first method proposed, the bias-variance method, which is strongly related to the commensurate prior approach, and a more recent and widely used approach called robust mixture priors (RMP).
findings.evidence: Abstract: unifies commensurate/Pocock and robust-mixture-prior borrowing frameworks.
findings.study_system: clinical trials (human); robust mixture prior vs commensurate/Pocock borrowing

findings.claim: A covariate-adjusted meta-analytic-predictive (CA-MAP) prior models covariate effects directly so the amount of historical control borrowing depends on the consistency of covariate effects across trials rather than on matching outcome summaries, allowing beneficial borrowing even when marginal outcomes differ.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this paper, we propose a covariate adjusted meta-analytic-predictive (CA-MAP) prior for historical control borrowing.
findings.evidence: Abstract: covariate-effect-based extension of MAP borrowing using patient-level data.
findings.study_system: clinical trials (human, patient-level data); covariate-adjusted MAP prior

findings.claim: A simulation study of propensity-score-integrated Bayesian borrowing (Power, Elastic and Mixture priors) for hybrid control arms finds the approach helps under selection bias but that unmeasured confounders, measurement error and effect drift undermine bias and Type I error control for methods relying solely on covariate similarity.

findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The aflibercept arm was exactly matched 1:1 with the bevacizumab trial arm on baseline confounders (age, sex, and visual acuity).
findings.study_system: neovascular age-related macular degeneration patients (ABC RCT vs EHR real-world controls)

findings.claim: External real-world control cohorts were used to estimate comparative efficacy for a single-arm oncology trial, yielding a large apparent treatment benefit versus the real-world control on progression-free survival.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Median PFS was not reached in the selpercatinib group (95% CI 11.5-not reached) versus 6.7 months (95% CI 3.7-12.1 months) for the real-world control.
findings.effect_size: median PFS not reached (selpercatinib) vs 6.7 months (95% CI 3.7-12.1) for real-world control
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Median PFS was not reached in the selpercatinib group (95% CI 11.5-not reached) versus 6.7 months (95% CI 3.7-12.1 months) for the real-world control.
findings.study_system: RET fusion-positive advanced/metastatic NSCLC (LIBRETTO-001 vs real-world external controls)

findings.claim: Synthetic controls derived from machine-learning predictions of standard-of-care recovery were proposed for rare, heterogeneous disorders, with a convolutional neural network achieving low prediction error and no significant difference versus randomized controls in a case study.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We identified a convolutional neural network as the best-performing architecture to predict segmental motor score sequences, achieving a median root mean squared error below the neurological level of injury of 0.55.
findings.effect_size: median RMSE 0.55 (below neurological level of injury)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We identified a convolutional neural network as the best-performing architecture to predict segmental motor score sequences, achieving a median root mean squared error below the neurological level of injury of 0.55.
findings.study_system: spinal cord injury patients (EMSCI n=4196; Sygen n=587)

findings.claim: The VICT3R international project reuses precompetitive shared corporate toxicology data (building on the eTOX and eTRANSAFE initiatives) to generate virtual control groups for nonclinical drug safety assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The VICT3R project is using these shared data for generating virtual control groups to be applied in nonclinical drug safety assessment.
findings.study_system: nonclinical drug safety data-sharing initiatives (eTOX, eTRANSAFE, VICT3R)

findings.claim: In soil mesofauna field studies, high control (background) abundance variability caused a statistical test (CPCAT) to flag significant differences in over half of comparisons even before treatment, which should be considered false positives, arguing for biological control ranges rather than statistics alone.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Significant differences were observed in more than 50% of the comparisons using CPCAT, even before test item application happened in the field.
findings.effect_size: >50% of comparisons significant (false positive) pre-application
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Significant differences were observed in more than 50% of the comparisons using CPCAT, even before test item application happened in the field.
findings.study_system: Collembola soil mesofauna field studies (ecological risk assessment of pesticides)

findings.claim: Requiring a joint significant trend-plus-pairwise (control vs high-dose) test in rodent carcinogenicity evaluation can massively inflate the false-negative rate relative to a trend test alone, unless significance levels are recalibrated.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The inflation can be as high as 204.5% of the false negative rate when the trend test alone is required to test if the effect is statistically significant.
findings.effect_size: up to 204.5% inflation of false-negative rate
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The inflation can be as high as 204.5% of the false negative rate when the trend test alone is required to test if the effect is statistically significant.
findings.study_system: rodent carcinogenicity studies (simulation, FDA)

findings.claim: A simulation of aquatic toxicity tests with two concurrent controls (water and solvent) found the solvent control alone, or conditional pooling, best balances false-positive rate and power, questioning whether both concurrent control groups are needed.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The evidence supports using either the solvent control only in all cases or a sequential strategy of combining the water and solvent controls unless the two controls are found to be statistically significantly different, in which case only the solvent control should be used.
findings.study_system: aquatic toxicology experiments with solvent carriers (simulation)

findings.claim: A simulation study compared false-positive rates of the Peto and Poly-K trend tests (with Lin-Rahman multiplicity adjustment) for long-term carcinogenicity control-versus-treated tumor comparisons, addressing how test choice affects false positives.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this work the authors compared the overall false positive rates of the Peto and Poly-K tests using the Lin-Rahman multiple comparison adjustment based on some simulation results.
findings.study_system: long-term (2-year) rodent carcinogenicity data (simulation)

findings.claim: In NTP rodent bioassays, about 92% of chemicals show a statistically significant tumor decrease at at least one site, a false-positive concern arising from random variability in background tumor rates and multiple control-versus-treated comparisons.
findings.claim_source_sentence: About 92% of chemicals tested by the National Toxicology Program prior to 1983 reveal at least one site with a significant (p < or = 0.05) tumor rate decrease in one or more tested groups, a result consistent with those of J. K. Haseman and F. M. Johnson (1996, Mutat. Res. 350, 131-141) for a database of recently tested chemicals.
findings.effect_size: ~92% of NTP chemicals show >=1 site with significant (p<=0.05) tumor-rate decrease
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: About 92% of chemicals tested by the National Toxicology Program prior to 1983 reveal at least one site with a significant (p < or = 0.05) tumor rate decrease in one or more tested groups, a result consistent with those of J. K. Haseman and F. M. Johnson (1996, Mutat. Res. 350, 131-141) for a database of recently tested chemicals.
findings.study_system: NTP rodent cancer bioassays (Monte-Carlo simulation)

findings.claim: Digital heart twins calibrated from preclinical swine data were used to simulate doxorubicin cardiotoxicity outcomes in silico, exemplifying virtual/computational approaches that could reduce reliance on live control and treated animals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our digital heart twins were directly calibrated and validated using measurements of conduction velocity and action potential wave features obtained via catheter-based electro-anatomical mapping after chemotherapy in preclinical swine models.
findings.study_system: preclinical swine (doxorubicin cardiotoxicity; 3D MRI-based computational models, 3 pigs)

findings.claim: A health-technology-assessment review round-up covers real-world data as a measure of treatment effectiveness in NICE submissions and a validation study of synthetic data, reflecting growing regulatory scrutiny of external and synthetic control evidence.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this update, we discuss recent publications examining the use of real-world data as a measure of treatment effectiveness in submissions to the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence, the results of a pilot study from the Coalition to Advance Real-World Evidence initiative and a validation study of synthetic data.
findings.study_system: health technology assessment / real-world and synthetic data (review)

findings.claim: An EMR-derived probable-clinical-trial cohort and a real-world external-control cohort in NSCLC showed no statistically significant overall-survival difference, supporting comparability of real-world external controls in this setting.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Median (standard deviation) OS was 10.2 (0.7) months for the RWD arm and 11.3 (1.3) for the probable CT arm with a Log rank p-value equal to 0.4771.
findings.effect_size: median OS 10.2 (SD 0.7) mo (RWD) vs 11.3 (1.3) mo (trial cohort), log-rank p=0.4771
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Median (standard deviation) OS was 10.2 (0.7) months for the RWD arm and 11.3 (1.3) for the probable CT arm with a Log rank p-value equal to 0.4771.
findings.study_system: non-small-cell lung cancer (EMR-derived cohorts as external control)

findings.claim: A covariate-adjusted meta-analytic-predictive Bayesian hierarchical approach combined with propensity scores was proposed to augment a concurrent control arm with external control data while accounting for prior-data conflict and covariate imbalance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this paper, we propose a Bayesian hierarchical modeling strategy incorporating covariate-adjusted meta-analytic predictive approach (cMAP) and also introduce a propensity score (PS) based sequential procedure that integrates the cMAP.
findings.study_system: clinical trial control-arm augmentation with external data (simulation)

findings.claim: In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, external controls built from historical RCT placebo arms reproduced the original trial's treatment effect, whereas external controls from real-world registry or EHR data did not, indicating the data source determines external-control validity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: IPF ECs generated from historical RCT placebo arms result in comparable primary treatment effects to that of the original clinical trial, whereas ECs from real-world data sources, including registry or EHR data, do not.
findings.effect_size: RCT-derived EC point estimates within original 95% CI; registry/EHR-derived ECs outside
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: RCT ECs showed treatment effect point estimates within the 95% CI of the original BMS-986020 RCT.
findings.study_system: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients (RCT, registry, and EHR external controls)

findings.claim: When synthetic-control-arm time-to-event data have disease-assessment schedules inconsistent with the trial, a multiple-imputation harmonization framework is needed; otherwise unadjusted external-control comparisons suffer severe type-I-error inflation or power loss.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We demonstrate through extensive simulations that the proposed framework is unbiased in estimating median TTE and hazard ratio, well controls the type I error and achieves desirable power for log-rank test, while the unadjusted analysis can be biased and suffer from severe type I error inflation or power loss depending on the direction of the bias.
findings.study_system: synthetic control arm progression-free survival comparisons (simulation)

findings.claim: A methodological roundtable concluded that single-arm studies should be replaced by formally externally controlled trials (per ICH E10), with the external control (historical, synthetic, or MAIC) and comparison method pre-specified in the protocol.
findings.claim_source_sentence: When these limitations are taken into account this should, first and foremost, lead to the conduct of externally controlled trials instead of single-arm trials as is proposed by the latest version of ICH E10.
findings.study_system: externally controlled trial methodology (expert roundtable / guidelines)

findings.claim: INHAND terminology is periodically revised (here ovarian sex cord/stromal lesions, 10 years after the 2014 female-reproductive publication), showing that the standardized nomenclature underpinning historical-control lesion comparisons is not static.
findings.claim_source_sentence: After 10 years of practical use, the scientific community requested from the organ working group (OWG) a review of the terminology and criteria for diagnosing ovarian sex cord/stromal lesions.
findings.study_system: rat and mouse female reproductive system (INHAND nomenclature revision)

findings.claim: The INHAND nonhuman-primate nomenclature standardizes classification of spontaneous (background) and test-material-induced microscopic lesions across tissues, drawing on pooled global histopathology databases - the reference framework that makes historical-control lesion data comparable.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The purpose of this publication is to provide a standardized nomenclature for classifying microscopic lesions observed in most tissues and organs from the nonhuman primate used in nonclinical safety studies.
findings.study_system: nonhuman primate (cynomolgus macaque) nonclinical safety studies (INHAND)

findings.claim: The INHAND minipig nomenclature provides a standardized classification of spontaneous and induced microscopic lesions built from government, academic, and industrial histopathology databases, supporting background/historical-control lesion documentation in this species.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The purpose of this publication is to provide a standardized nomenclature for classifying microscopic lesions observed in most tissues and organs from the minipig used in nonclinical safety studies.
findings.study_system: minipig nonclinical safety studies (INHAND)

findings.claim: The INHAND dog nomenclature standardizes classification of spontaneous and induced lesions from pooled international histopathology databases, providing the common language needed to reuse background/historical-control pathology across dog studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The purpose of this publication is to provide a standardized nomenclature for classifying lesions observed in most tissues and organs from the dog used in nonclinical safety studies.
findings.study_system: dog nonclinical safety studies (INHAND)

findings.claim: Of anticancer products approved in the EU on single-arm trials, external controls are noted as a way to contextualize results but carry limitations that must be addressed.
findings.claim_source_sentence: External controls may facilitate in the contextualization process, but the associated limitations must be addressed.
findings.evidence: Review of EU anticancer approvals based on single-arm trials (SATs); external controls used to contextualize benefit magnitude via ESMO-MCBS.
findings.effect_size: 18 products approved on 21 SATs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Eighteen medicinal products were approved based on 21 SATs-few medicinal products were supported by >1 SAT.
findings.study_system: EU (EMA) anticancer marketing authorizations based on single-arm trials

findings.claim: Externally controlled trials face data challenges because real-world data on testing timing/process differ from trial protocols, biasing comparisons.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Even where data may be recorded and decisions made consistent with clinical trials, there may be differences with respect to the timing and process of testing, which may influence the availability of testing.
findings.evidence: Viewpoint enumerating identification, outcome, and time-selection challenges when using RWD as an external control arm for single-arm trials.
findings.study_system: Real-world data external control arms (methodology viewpoint)

findings.claim: Across seven oncology external control arm case studies, selection bias and confounding were the most common critiques, but regulators and HTA bodies rarely agreed on their critiques.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Across case studies, selection bias and confounding were the most common ECA critiques.
findings.evidence: Comparison of 7 oncology ECA case studies evaluated by FDA/EMA/Health Canada and HTA agencies; low inter-agency agreement on critiques.
findings.study_system: Regulatory/HTA evaluations of 7 oncology external control arms

findings.claim: Across 20 notable regulatory applications using patient-level RWD as external controls, regulatory decisions were strongly influenced by the quality and usability of the RWD.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Regulatory decisions were strongly influenced by the quality and usability of the RWD.
findings.evidence: Review of 20 oncology/rare-disease licensing applications contextualizing single-arm trials with patient-level RWD external controls.
findings.effect_size: 20 applications
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This review focuses on 20 notable new drug or biologic licensing applications that included patient-level RWD or other external data for contextualization of trial results.
findings.study_system: Regulatory applications using RWD external controls (oncology, rare disease)

findings.claim: RWD-based external control groups can be highly informative when well conducted and designed to balance patient characteristics, e.g., replicating an RCT while controlling for >120 confounders by propensity matching.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In their study, the authors identified the patient population by adapting eligibility criteria from the CAROLINA study and by using propensity score matching to control for >120 potential confounding variables.
findings.evidence: Review of RWD external control arms in oncology drug development; describes replication of the CAROLINA RCT using US claims data with propensity matching.
findings.effect_size: >120 potential confounding variables
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In their study, the authors identified the patient population by adapting eligibility criteria from the CAROLINA study and by using propensity score matching to control for >120 potential confounding variables.
findings.study_system: Oncology external control groups from real-world data

findings.claim: Beyond regulatory external control arms, biopharma leverages RWE across the development process to inform pipeline, trial design, endpoints and sample size.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although much of the recent literature on RWE has focused on potential regulatory uses (e.g., product approvals in oncology or rare diseases based on single-arm trials with external control arms), this article reviews how biopharmaceutical companies can leverage RWE to inform internal decisions made throughout the product development process.
findings.evidence: Review of real-world evidence uses in drug development including external control arms and Bayesian priors.
findings.study_system: Real-world evidence in biopharmaceutical drug development

findings.claim: In a systematic review of 2015-2020 FDA oncology approvals, only 11 of 133 original approvals (8.3%) used RWE for efficacy, all retrospective, with a mean IND-to-approval time of 5.7 years.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Among these, 11 (8.3%) included RWE in support of efficacy with an average time from IND submission to approval of 5.7 years.
findings.evidence: Systematic review of FDA oncology NDA/BLA approvals; RWE external controls complemented single-arm efficacy in successful approvals but drew FDA critiques on confounding and RECIST comparability.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Among these, 11 (8.3%) included RWE in support of efficacy with an average time from IND submission to approval of 5.7 years.
findings.study_system: FDA oncology product approvals 2015-2020 using real-world evidence

findings.claim: Hybrid trial designs supplementing single-arm data with RWD-derived external comparators have already succeeded in some regulatory decisions, raising the prospect of augmenting or replacing RCTs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Some of these approaches have already been successfully used in regulatory decisions, raising the possibility that studies using RWD could increasingly be used to augment or replace traditional RCTs for the demonstration of drug effectiveness in certain contexts.
findings.evidence: Review of hybrid RCT/RWD trial designs including external comparators for regulatory decision-making.
findings.study_system: Hybrid trial designs using real-world data (regulatory)

findings.claim: The SEND standard for nonclinical data is FDA-required but its implementation guide's flexibility produces significant variability across datasets, hampering cross-study reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The SEND Implementation Guide (SENDIG) allows for considerable flexibility in how data is represented; interpretation of these guidelines has led to significant variability in the approach to SEND dataset creation.
findings.evidence: Proposal to harmonize SEND datasets to enable cross-study analysis of warehoused nonclinical toxicology control data.
findings.study_system: SEND (Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Data) toxicology datasets

findings.claim: A synthetic control arm built from mixed clinical-trial and real-world data for elderly DLBCL patients reproduced an RCT control arm, with no significant survival difference vs the SENIOR experimental arm.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In newly diagnosed elderly DLBCL patients, the use of SCAs can mimic the control arm of an RCT and could be used to build comparative CT for elderly patients and come up with fast-innovative CTs.
findings.evidence: Mixed synthetic control arm (LNH09-7B trial + REALYSA real-world) for >=80 y DLBCL, balanced by stabilized IPTW on propensity scores.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: OS of Mixed SCA vs. SENIOR experimental arm were not statistically different, with a HR of 0.743 [0.494-1.118] (p = 0.1654).
findings.study_system: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (>=80 y) synthetic control arm

findings.claim: A real-world synthetic control arm for relapsed SCLC estimated a survival benefit of lurbinectedin vs historical standard of care (adjusted HR 0.61).
findings.claim_source_sentence: The adjusted hazard ratio comparing lurbinectedin with the historical standard of care (referent group) was 0.61 (95% CI 0.45-0.82; unadjusted HR: 0.72; 95% CI 0.54-0.97).
findings.evidence: Synthetic control arm from Alberta real-world databases (n=174) vs single-arm lurbinectedin trial (n=105); Cox model adjusted for CTFI and stage.
findings.effect_size: adjusted HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.45-0.82)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The adjusted hazard ratio comparing lurbinectedin with the historical standard of care (referent group) was 0.61 (95% CI 0.45-0.82; unadjusted HR: 0.72; 95% CI 0.54-0.97).
findings.study_system: Relapsed small cell lung cancer synthetic control arm (real-world)

findings.claim: A real-world synthetic comparator was used as an external control for the single-arm TRANSCEND trial to compare liso-cel with conventional therapies in relapsed/refractory LBCL.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This study used a real-world population as a synthetic comparator for the single-arm TRANSCEND NHL 001 study (TRANSCEND; NCT02631044) to evaluate the efficacy of lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) compared with conventional (noncellular) therapies in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL).
findings.evidence: Propensity-matched real-world synthetic control (n=257 per arm) vs single-arm CAR-T trial data.
findings.study_system: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma synthetic control (CAR-T)

findings.claim: An automated deep-learning propensity method (BCAUS) balances covariates across arbitrarily many observational intervention arms, tested on a diabetes dataset of over 100,000 individuals across >100 arms.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We tested BCAUS on the semi-synthetic Infant Health & Development Program dataset with a single intervention arm, and a real-world observational study of diabetes interventions with over 100,000 individuals spread across more than a hundred intervention arms.
findings.evidence: Methods paper for scalable propensity-score covariate balancing in massive multi-arm observational comparisons.
findings.effect_size: >100,000 individuals; >100 arms
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We tested BCAUS on the semi-synthetic Infant Health & Development Program dataset with a single intervention arm, and a real-world observational study of diabetes interventions with over 100,000 individuals spread across more than a hundred intervention arms.
findings.study_system: Multi-arm observational causal inference (propensity balancing)

findings.claim: Choosing statistically efficient designs and the most powerful analysis for relative-potency assays is framed as an ethical requirement because experiments involve animal sacrifice, and enables animal reduction.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Using the most powerful statistical designs and analyses is always preferred, but is an ethical requirement when experiments involve animal sacrifice.
findings.evidence: Simulation comparison of five interval estimators of relative potency; Wald intervals in equal-response designs give best power and near-nominal coverage at small n, reducing animal numbers.
findings.effect_size: coverage 97.1% at n=24
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Fieller's CIs held the nominal 95% level most closely among all the methods, not deviating by more than 0.5 percentage points when sample sizes were >=40, and was 97.1% for the smallest sample size of 24.
findings.study_system: Parallel-line quantal assays (toxicology / radiation countermeasure animal studies)

findings.claim: A critical re-evaluation of a rodent carcinogenicity bioassay stresses that proper interpretation requires attention to multiple comparisons and to both concurrent and historical controls.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This involves attention to study details, including reliable histopathologic diagnoses, and proper statistical analyses, including consideration of multiple comparisons, concurrent and historical controls.
findings.evidence: Re-analysis of JBRC n-butyl methacrylate 2-year bioassays; concludes tumor increases are consistent with chance and not treatment-related, contra IARC 2B classification.
findings.study_system: n-butyl methacrylate rodent carcinogenicity bioassay (rats, mice)

findings.claim: An expert-panel weight-of-evidence review of glyphosate carcinogenicity discounted a significant high-dose tumor increase because it fell within the historical control range.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Glyphosate has been rigorously and extensively tested for carcinogenicity by administration to mice (five studies) and to rats (nine studies).
findings.evidence: Expert panel reassessed IARC's glyphosate data; used historical control ranges and dose-response/consistency criteria to conclude glyphosate is not a carcinogen in laboratory animals.
findings.effect_size: 5 mouse studies; 9 rat studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Glyphosate has been rigorously and extensively tested for carcinogenicity by administration to mice (five studies) and to rats (nine studies).
findings.study_system: Glyphosate rodent carcinogenicity (mouse and rat bioassays)

findings.claim: Supplementing a small historical control database with 25 additional matched-diet studies widened tumor-incidence ranges and thereby weakened, to 'no' evidence, the carcinogenicity signal for vanadium pentoxide in rats.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This widened the HC tumor incidence ranges, thereby weakening the limited evidence for the carcinogenicity of inhaled V(2)O(5) in rats relative to HCs.
findings.evidence: Re-analysis of NTP vanadium pentoxide bioassay; expanded NTP-2000 diet HCD reclassified 'some/equivocal' evidence to 'no' evidence, and flagged the study's own male control as a near-outlier.
findings.effect_size: 25 additional studies added to HCD
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We supplemented the early NTP-2000 diet HC data with data from 25 additional NTP-2000 diet studies conducted subsequent to the V(2)O(5) bioassay.
findings.study_system: Vanadium pentoxide carcinogenicity in F344/N rats (historical controls)

findings.claim: In rodent cancer bioassays the concurrent control is the most relevant comparator, with historical control data useful only in specific situations and as one input to a weight-of-evidence assessment; range statistics are highly outlier-sensitive.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While the concurrent control group provides the most relevant control data for determining treatment-related effects in a study, evaluation of HCD may be useful in certain situations.
findings.evidence: Points-to-consider paper; recommends median/IQR boxplots over range/mean/SD for HCD, using Poly-3 survival-adjusted rates, because the range is dominated by single outlier studies.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: These studies had a mean of 3.31%, a standard deviation of 6.47% and a range of 0% to 34% for all routes and vehicles.
findings.study_system: NTP rodent carcinogenicity historical control data (B6C3F1 mice)

findings.claim: Body-growth rate strongly influences background liver tumor incidence in B6C3F1 mice, so dietary control of body weight standardizes background tumor incidence and predicts a terminal background rate of 15-20%.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In B6C3F1 mice, the rate of body growth influences susceptibility to liver neoplasia and large variations in body weight can complicate the interpretation of bioassay data.
findings.evidence: Historical control populations (~2,750 male, ~2,300 female mice) used to build idealized weight curves; dietary-controlled mice matched predicted background tumor rates.
findings.effect_size: terminal background liver tumor incidence 15-20%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Resulting tumor risk data were then used to construct idealized weight curves for male and female B6C3F1 mice; these curves predict a terminal background liver tumor incidence of 15-20%.
findings.study_system: B6C3F1 mouse chronic bioassay background liver tumor incidence

findings.claim: Interpreting a chronic bioassay of D5 depended on which of four historical control sets (varying heterogeneity) was used, showing HCD-choice sensitivity in a marginal carcinogenicity call.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Four sets of (historical) control groups were formed, with varying heterogeneity.
findings.evidence: Statistical re-analysis of D5 uterine endometrial adenocarcinoma; effect at 160 ppm was significant or borderline depending on control set and whether the high dose was included.
findings.effect_size: 160 ppm: 5/60 cases vs control 0/60
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Four groups of 60 Fischer-344 female rats were analyzed for uterine endometrial adenocarcinoma (inhalation study with exposure levels in ppm/number of observed cases: 0/0, 10/1, 40/0, and 160/5) by exact regression (logistic, Poisson), the max poly-3 trend test, and a random effects probit model.
findings.study_system: Decamethylcyclopentasiloxane (D5) F344 rat uterine adenocarcinoma bioassay

findings.claim: NTP historical control tumor rates differ markedly between rat strains: female Sprague Dawley vs F344/N rats differ ~18-fold in mononuclear cell leukemia background (0.9% vs 16.7%), undermining cross-strain control reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our analyses revealed statistically significant strain differences, with female SD rats having lower incidence rates for clitoral gland adenoma (0.2% vs. 5.8%) and mononuclear cell leukemia (0.9% vs. 16.7%) and higher incidence rates for mammary gland fibroadenoma (67.4% vs. 48.4%), mammary gland carcinoma (10.2% vs. 2.4%), and thyroid gland C cell adenoma (25.4% vs. 13.6%) relative to female F344/N rats.
findings.evidence: Comparison of NTP historical control tumor incidence between nine female SD rat studies and matched F344/N studies.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Our analyses revealed statistically significant strain differences, with female SD rats having lower incidence rates for clitoral gland adenoma (0.2% vs. 5.8%) and mononuclear cell leukemia (0.9% vs. 16.7%) and higher incidence rates for mammary gland fibroadenoma (67.4% vs. 48.4%), mammary gland carcinoma (10.2% vs. 2.4%), and thyroid gland C cell adenoma (25.4% vs. 13.6%) relative to female F344/N rats.
findings.study_system: NTP historical control data, female SD vs F344/N rats

findings.claim: The F344 rat's highly variable spontaneous mononuclear cell leukemia background led NTP to change stocks and warrants greater-than-usual reliance on historical control data to interpret treatment effects.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We show that due to the highly variable background incidence of F344 MNCL, more reliance on historical control data than is usual for most tumor responses is warranted to evaluate potential effect of any chemical treatment in this rat strain.
findings.evidence: Retrospective review of F344 MNCL, Leydig cell tumors and tunica vaginalis mesothelioma; high/variable spontaneous backgrounds reduce human relevance and complicate control comparisons.
findings.study_system: F344 rat cancer bioassay spontaneous tumors (NTP)

findings.claim: In a 2-year inhalation bioassay, several tumor incidences that exceeded the Japan Bioassay Research Center historical control range were treated as evidence of carcinogenicity for 1,1,1-trichloroethane.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Thus, this study provided clear evidence of inhalation carcinogenicity for TCE in both rats and mice.
findings.evidence: TCE inhalation bioassay in F344 rats and BDF1 mice; tumor increases (e.g., bronchiolo-alveolar adenomas at 3200 ppm, malignant lymphomas) exceeded JBRC historical control ranges.
findings.study_system: 1,1,1-trichloroethane inhalation carcinogenicity (F344 rats, BDF1 mice)

findings.claim: A predictive-distribution power-prior method estimates the borrowing parameter so that type I error is controlled by calibrating to the similarity of new and historical control data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The method is based on predictive distributions and parameterized in such a way that the type I error can be controlled by calibrating to the degree of similarity between the new and historical data.
findings.evidence: Empirical power prior for dynamic borrowing from a single historical control study while controlling type I error.
findings.study_system: Statistical methodology; single historical control dataset, normal outcomes

findings.claim: In hybrid designs augmenting an RCT with external controls via power priors, prior-data conflict risks biasing treatment-effect estimates and can distort conclusions.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, the use of external control data poses a risk of introducing bias, particularly in the presence of prior-data conflict, which can distort treatment effect estimates.
findings.evidence: Constrained power-prior borrowing to control type I error in hybrid designs.

findings.claim: When a uniformly most powerful test exists, strict type I error control means external-information borrowing yields no power gain, undercutting a central justification for dynamic borrowing.

establishing.thesis: Reusing historical control-animal data as virtual control groups (VCGs) converts abstract data reuse into concrete Reduction - roughly a quarter fewer control animals - and the infrastructure to do it already exists at scale. But the payoff is conditional: concordance with concurrent controls is endpoint-dependent, temporal and cross-laboratory drift can bias conclusions, and no regulator has yet accepted a VCG-based study, so the ethical dividend remains partly theoretical.
establishing.synthesis: VCGs reuse animal data to reduce animal use; sec-nams-data addresses the complementary strategy - replacing animals with non-animal methods - and shows those methods generate their own data that must be stewarded to avoid re-incurring the debt.
